nodes.task: Open the journal.
nodes.story:
This journal records everything you learn about the sky. New pages appear on their own as soon as you discover something. The way to other worlds begins with a simple question: what is up there?

If the journal is lost, a new one can be made from a book and lapis lazuli: the records are kept not in it but in your memory, and the new journal will open on the same page.

nodes.task: Make a polished lens. Mix sand, an amethyst shard and clay into glass blend and smelt it into optical glass. Four pieces make a lens blank. Polish the blank with grinding paste and a piece of wool.
nodes.story: Ordinary glass is cloudy and bends light unevenly. Optical glass is made from a pure blend, and the lens is ground by hand until it gathers light into a single point.

nodes.task: Build a telescope from four parts: an optical tube, an eyepiece, a mount head and a tripod. The tube and the eyepiece each need a polished lens; tubes and gears are made from copper sheets.
nodes.story: A refractor gathers light with a lens at the front of the tube. Galileo looked at the sky through one just like it — and saw mountains on the Moon.

nodes.task: Place the telescope under the open sky and look through it at night.
nodes.story:
Astronomers call the first look through a new telescope its first light. Bright stars of the same color often belong to one constellation: select a star and then another to draw a line between them.

If the figure does not come together, the telescope will find one missing line for you in exchange for stardust. Stardust comes from shooting stars: aim at one and left-click before it burns out. Every discovery in the sky brings some as well.

nodes.task: Find the Moon in the telescope, aim at it and hold the left mouse button until the image becomes sharp.
nodes.story: Dark seas of frozen lava, bright highlands and countless craters. Under the seas there are tunnels left by lava rivers, and moonstone glimmers at the bottom of the craters.
nodes.facts:
Distance from Earth: 384,400 km
Day: 29.5 Earth days
Gravity: 0.17 of Earth's

nodes.task: Find seven bluish stars in the shape of a dipper and connect them: the four stars of the bowl into a closed quadrangle, the three stars of the handle into a chain leading away from it.
nodes.story: The best-known figure of the northern sky. The two stars at the edge of the dipper point to the North Star, and Mizar in the handle has been used to test eyesight since ancient times.

nodes.task: Find the red star Antares and connect the stars around it into a scorpion with a curved tail.
nodes.story: Antares is a red supergiant hundreds of times wider than the Sun. Its name means "rival of Mars": the red planet often passes nearby, and the two are easy to confuse.

nodes.task: Find three stars in a row — the belt of Orion — and complete the figure of the hunter.
nodes.story: Orange Betelgeuse at the shoulder, blue Rigel at the foot. Below the belt there is a hazy spot: the Orion Nebula, where new stars are being born right now.
A cold desert the color of rust. Canyons with layered walls, the tallest volcanoes in the Solar System and polar caps of dry ice. Sunsets there are blue.
nodes.facts:
Distance from the Sun: 228 million km
Day: 24 h 37 min
Gravity: 0.38 of Earth's

nodes.task: Build a reflector: an eyepiece, a truss tube, a primary mirror and an equatorial mount are added to the old refractor. The mirror is made of two lens blanks and coated with mirror coating.
nodes.story: A mirror is easier to make large than a lens, and the larger it is, the fainter the stars it shows. The first telescope of this kind was built by Isaac Newton.

nodes.task: Find orange Aldebaran — the eye of the bull — and draw the horns from it.
nodes.story: Near the tip of one horn a star exploded in 1054; for several weeks it was visible even in daytime. The Crab Nebula remains in its place.

nodes.task: Find two bright stars side by side, Castor and Pollux, and draw the figures of the twins.
nodes.story: Castor looks like a single star, but in fact it is six stars circling one another.

nodes.task: Find blue Regulus and the sickle of stars above it — the mane of the lion.
nodes.story: Regulus spins so fast that it is flattened like a pumpkin. If it spun a little faster, it would fly apart.
Under the clouds lies the hottest world in the Solar System: volcanoes, rivers of lava and peaks covered with metallic frost. The Sun rises there in the west.
nodes.facts:
Distance from the Sun: 108 million km
Day: 117 Earth days
Gravity: 0.90 of Earth's

nodes.story: The planet closest to the Sun. By day stone glows with heat there, and in the craters at the poles, where sunlight never reaches, ice has been lying for billions of years.
nodes.facts:
Distance from the Sun: 58 million km
Day: 176 Earth days
Gravity: 0.38 of Earth's

nodes.story: A giant without a surface: clouds upon clouds for thousands of kilometers down. The Great Red Spot is a storm larger than the Earth that has been raging for centuries.
nodes.facts:
Distance from the Sun: 778 million km
Day: 9 h 56 min
Gravity: 2.53 of Earth's

nodes.task: Make the astrograph: a moonstone lens, an imaging plate and a star tracker are added to the reflector. It is too heavy for a tripod. Lay a base of nine plates, put a pier in the middle and the astrograph on top.
nodes.story: The sky turns, and stars drift out of view. The tracker turns the telescope after them, and the plate gathers light for hours — this is how things the eye cannot see are revealed.

nodes.task: Find eight golden stars in the shape of a teapot.
nodes.story: The center of our Galaxy lies in this direction. The Milky Way is brightest here and seems to rise from the spout of the teapot like steam.

nodes.task: Find the turquoise stars of Aquarius: a bright pair and a small jug beside them.
nodes.story: Almost all the stars of Aquarius bear names that mean luck: Sadalsuud is "luckiest of the lucky".

nodes.task: Find two chains of faint violet stars that meet at an angle, and close a ring at the end of each.
nodes.story: Two fish tied together with a ribbon. The star Alrescha — "the cord" — is the knot that joins them.
The rings are made of countless pieces of ice, from dust specks to boulders the size of a house. At the north pole a storm in the shape of a regular hexagon has been spinning for decades.
nodes.facts:
Distance from the Sun: 1.43 billion km
Day: 10 h 33 min
Gravity: 1.07 of Earth's

nodes.story: An ice giant lying on its side: it rolls along its orbit like a ball. Deep below the clouds the pressure turns methane into diamonds, and they fall like rain.
nodes.facts:
Distance from the Sun: 2.87 billion km
Day: 17 h 14 min
Gravity: 0.89 of Earth's

nodes.story: The farthest planet. The fastest winds in the Solar System blow there — faster than sound. Neptune was first found by calculation and only then seen through a telescope.
nodes.facts:
Distance from the Sun: 4.5 billion km
Day: 16 h 6 min
Gravity: 1.14 of Earth's

nodes.task: Make the graviscope: two resonance rings and a gravity core are added to the astrograph. Take the astrograph off its pier (the base stays): the graviscope stands on the same base and pier, with four gravity pylons at the corners.
nodes.story: Some things give off no light at all, but anything that has mass bends space around itself. The graviscope sees these bends — which means it sees what cannot be seen.

nodes.task: Find white Deneb and draw a cross from it: the body of the swan and its spread wings.
nodes.story: Deneb is one of the most powerful stars that can be seen with the naked eye: it shines like tens of thousands of Suns. Albireo at the beak is a double star, gold and blue.
The first black hole ever found. It circles a blue supergiant and pulls gas off it; as the gas falls, it heats up to millions of degrees and shines in X-rays.
nodes.facts:
Distance: 7,200 light-years
Mass: 21 Suns
Event horizon: 124 km across

nodes.story: A supermassive black hole around which the whole Galaxy turns. Stars near it fly at thousands of kilometers per second — it was by their orbits that its mass was measured.
nodes.facts:
Distance: 26,000 light-years
Mass: 4.3 million Suns
Event horizon: 25 million km across

nodes.task: Make the magmascope: a heatproof lens, a deep bell and a magma core on a blackstone base. In the Nether, lay a three-by-three slab of scorched plating, put the magmascope in the middle and heatproof piers two blocks tall on the corners. When the structure assembles, pour three buckets of lava into the bowl.
nodes.story:
The Nether has no sky: there is stone overhead. But underfoot, beneath the floor of the lava seas, lies bottomless magma, and there are hollows in it — vents with other worlds at the bottom. Magma lets no light through, and eyes find nothing in it. The magmascope strikes it with a bell and listens: where it is hollow below, the strike comes back as an echo.

Fire bubbles rise through the magma: when one passes through the sight, click to catch a deep ember; finding a vent brings four. Three embers buy the toll (the hint key): it shows the nearest vent. Deep embers pay the gates of the worlds below the vents.

nodes.task: Look into the magmascope in the Nether: it stands on its plate with piers at the corners, three buckets of lava in the bowl. Find the vent of the Forge: strike the magma and follow the echo. Its pulse is the even blows of a hammer. Crack the crust by striking in time.
nodes.story: A vent lined with masonry and bound in gold: someone built it on purpose. At the bottom lies a sea of molten gold with islands of netherite slag adrift on it. They say the piglins carried their first gold out of here — and have not been able to forget its shine since.
nodes.facts:
A sea of molten gold
Islands of netherite slag
Forges whose fires were never put out

nodes.task: Find the vent of the Ash: strike the magma and follow the echo. Its pulse is two beats and a long silence, like a sigh. Crack the crust by striking in time.
nodes.story: A crater with crumbled edges. At the bottom is a desert of soul sand with ribs the size of a fortress sticking out of it. A blue flame burns over the sand — sulfur burns like that on the Ijen volcano on Earth, only here it is memories that burn. The lights rise and go out before they reach the top.
nodes.facts:
A desert of soul sand
A blue flame that gives no warmth
Ribs of giants instead of mountains

nodes.task: Find the vent of the Mycelium: strike the magma and follow the echo. Its pulse is three beats and a pause. Crack the crust by striking in time.
nodes.story: A vent overgrown from within. The crimson and the warped forest here are a single creature: a mycelium the size of a world. Its growths are joined by glowing threads with light running along them — that is how it thinks. On Earth fungi, too, are linked underground into webs as wide as forests; here the web has become everything there is.
nodes.facts:
One fungus the size of a world
Crimson and warped growths
Glowing threads instead of rivers

nodes.task: Find the vent of the Lament: strike the magma and follow the echo. Its pulse is uneven, like dripping water. Crack the crust by striking in time.
nodes.story: A splintered hole in black glass. The world at the bottom is all obsidian — frozen volcanic glass — and it weeps: glowing violet tears creep down its facets. On Earth such drops of cooled lava are called Pele's tears. Here they never cool.
nodes.facts:
A world of volcanic glass
Violet tears run down its facets
The weeping is heard through the magma

nodes.task: Make the bell dome and build the bell in the Nether over a pool of lava at least three by three: skirt, dome, crown, and a winch on top — the layout is below; put the skirt right onto the lava, and it will stand just above the surface. A cryo still distills coolant from ice and magma cream: click the bell with a coolant canister, or pipe the coolant to a launch gantry by the winch. Put an ember-tempered chain into the dome — an iron chain fired with a deep ember — and climb in.
nodes.story: The bell sinks into the lava on its chain and comes out at the bottom of a vent, in another world, still hanging from the chain. Coolant keeps the dome bearable; every dive from the Nether burns one ember-tempered chain — an ordinary chain would go soft in the lava — and the way back is free: the winch hauls the bell home. Where it may go is decided by the modules in its four sockets: the Forge takes it as it is, the other worlds need a heat belt, a slag jacket or a damper, each made of what the worlds before them yield.

nodes.task: Build the bell over a lava pool from the layout on the Diving Bell page: the skirt right onto the lava, then the dome, crown and winch on it. Click the bell with a coolant canister and an ember-tempered chain, then with an empty hand — Climb in, pick the Forge on the vent chart and dive. It is hot below: put a Cooling Unit into the spacesuit torso.
nodes.story: A sea of molten gold, islands of netherite slag, spires of living gold. It is hot: a suit with a Cooling Unit is a must. The bell hangs on its chain here: climb in again to be hauled home. Living gold and slag are needed for the heat belt and the slag jacket.

nodes.task: Beat the master of the Forge: he works at the bottom of the Gilded Deeps, and the elder of the Gilded sells a chart to it. Three locked gates bar the way down — each has its own riddle; lay two gold hearts on the master's anvil; gilded knights drop them. The first sign of the fight is a glowing circle on the floor: step out before the anvil falls.
nodes.story: The master of the guild that came down for adamant: when no fire could forge it, he made fire alive, and at last lay down under his own hammer. In battle his armor heats like metal in a forge — red-hot, then white-hot, and after he strikes himself, tempered blue. His heart of living gold goes into the heat belt of the diving bell and wakes the gate of the Forge, and the Master's Hammer is forged around it; the slag jacket of the bell is cut to the pattern of his scorched apron, which he leaves behind as well. Beyond the anvil the master's treasury opens.

nodes.task: Make a heat belt of living gold from the Forge and fit it into a socket on the bell dome.
nodes.story: The soul fire of the Ash draws warmth out of everything; living gold gives it back. With the belt the bell may dive to the Ash.

nodes.task: Make a slag jacket of netherite slag from the Forge, cut to the pattern of the Gilded Smith's scorched apron — the smith drops it along with his heart — and fit it into a socket on the bell dome.
nodes.story: The spores of the Mycelium root in anything they touch — except slag: nothing grows on it. With the jacket the bell may dive to the Mycelium.

nodes.task: Fit the heat belt and take the bell down the vent of the Ash. It is cold below: put a Heating Unit into the spacesuit torso.
nodes.story: A desert of soul ash under ribs of giants, lit by soul fire that gives no warmth. It is cold: a suit with a Heating Unit is a must. Soul cinder is needed for the damper.

nodes.task: Beat the master of the Ash: he lies in the floor of the Giant's Bier at the bottom of the Giant's Ossuary, and the Giantkin elder sells a chart to it. Three locked gates bar the way down — each has its own riddle; lay two soul embers on the altar on his chest; ash wraiths drop them. The first sign of the fight is his swing: get behind him.
nodes.story: One of the giants whose skeletons lie across the Ash stood up: for a hundred years its keepers poured blue marrow into its chest, until the chest caught a fire that does not warm but draws the warmth out of the living. In every phase he changes: the fire drinks the warmth and frost covers his bones; then the fire breaks out — the ribs open, a crown of flame rises over the skull and the broken horn grows back as a ghost of blue fire; at last the bone burns through to cold cinder, the jaw falls away, the bronze bands burst and fire gushes from the old fracture. His marrow wakes the gate of the Ash, and the damper of the diving bell and the Giant's Spine are built around it; beyond the altar the reliquary of the keepers opens.

nodes.task: Fit the slag jacket and take the bell down the vent of the Mycelium. There is no air below: wear the full spacesuit, filled at an oxygen tank.
nodes.story: One fungus the size of a world: crimson and warped growths, glowing threads in the hollows between them, and giant mushrooms above — titans, umbrellas and elders taller than trees, shelf fungi on stumps, lanterns with glowing gills. There is no air. Fungal felt is needed for the damper.

nodes.task: Beat the mistress of the Mycelium: she fruits in the deepest chamber of the Spore Deeps under the first bell, and the elder of the Fruiting Folk sells a chart to it. Three locked gates bar the way down — each has its own riddle; lay four spore dusts on the altar by the stump; spore puffs drop them. The first sign of the fight: her blows drink the air of your tank — come with a full one.
nodes.story: The fruit that the deepest flesh of the world-mycelium bore for the colonists: they fed it copper and their dead and begged it to fruit, and it grew them a cap that walks, never falls and gives nothing back to the threads. In every phase she changes: teal mycelium overgrows her crimson cap and sprouts horns of roots, then the cap opens into an amber flower. Her heart, the Mother Spore, wakes the gate of the Mycelium, and the Fruiting Staff grows from it; beyond the altar the seed vault opens.

nodes.task: Make a damper of fungal felt from the Mycelium and soul cinder from the Ash and fit it into a socket on the bell dome.
nodes.story: The Lament cries, and the crying cracks glass and bronze alike. Felt swallows the sound; cinder keeps the felt from burning. With the damper the bell may dive to the Lament.

nodes.task: Fit the damper and take the bell down the vent of the Lament.
nodes.story: Shard mountains of dark glass, veins and pools of glowing tears. Gravity is heavier than on Earth. Pele's tears grow here — and the bell can go no deeper.

nodes.task: Beat the mistress of the Lament: she waits by the last lake at the bottom of the Tear Deeps, and the Mourner elder sells a chart to it. Three locked gates bar the way down — each has its own riddle; lay two tear drops on the altar before her empty plinth; tear drinkers drop them. The first sign of the fight is the circle where her tears pour down: walk out before grief crushes you.
nodes.story: The statue that wept first: the lakes of the Lament are her tears, and the weight of the world is her grief. In every phase she changes: she tears off her hood and burns crimson, then her tears run dry and she fades to salt with the reliquary's vessels circling her, and at last what is left of them sprouts as turquoise sorrow quartz. Her Heart of Sorrow wakes the gate of the Lament, and the Rod of Sorrow cages it; beyond the altar the treasury with the Great Vessel opens.

nodes.task: Make the riftscope: two resonance rings, a void lens, two End resonators and a rift core in a purpur frame. In the End, build it a five-by-five base of void plating with a rift socket in the middle of each side and a two-block void pier; the riftscope goes on top. When the structure assembles, set an eye of ender into each of the four sockets.
nodes.story:
The sky of the End is not a sky. It is a thin film of void, and there are tears in it: behind each, another world. The riftscope gathers no light — its four eyes of ender look where all endermen look and show where the film is thinnest. Sparks of the void drift toward the rifts on their own: follow them.

Cracks open in the void now and then: aim at one and click before it closes for a void shard; finding a rift brings four. Three shards buy the call (the hint key): it shows the nearest rift and sends every spark to it. Void shards also spin the thread of the shuttle and pay the gates of the worlds beyond the rifts.

nodes.task: Find the rift of the Facet: the sparks flying to it turn lilac, and crystal light seeps through the seam. Tear the seam open.
nodes.story: A world inside a crystal. Everything in it is glass, light and reflection: clear plateaus with the layers below showing through, mirror canyons, kaleidoscope caves. Whole mountains are a single crystal with inclusions: the ore is visible from outside, but it can only be mined from the right side.
nodes.facts:
A world inside a crystal
Glass, light and reflections
Mountains of a single crystal

nodes.task: Find the rift of the Hive: the sparks near it blush pink, and the seam smells of chorus. Tear the seam open.
nodes.story: The homeland of the shulkers. A world built entirely of giant purpur combs, stacked into mountains and columns. The cells are hollow: inside are halls, passages and storerooms with loot. Between the combs are chasms of air, but there is always a floor: soft chorus wax that you fall into without harm and slowly sink in.
nodes.facts:
Homeland of the shulkers
Giant purpur combs
Chorus wax at the bottom of every chasm

nodes.task: Find the rift of the Breath: the sparks burn violet there, and the sky around it shimmers like air over a fire. Tear the seam open.
nodes.story: Everything the dragon has breathed out over thousands of years has gathered into one world. There is no solid ground: violet vapor rolls to the horizon, and islands of hardened breath float in it — glass that burns the skin. Lightning strikes between the islands, and on the islands grow the crystals that hold them up. The vapor eats through any suit without a coating.
nodes.facts:
The dragon's breath, gathered
Islands of burning glass in violet vapor
Lightning between them

nodes.task: Find the rift of the Eye: the sparks near it turn green, and the ripple around it blinks, as if something were watching back. Tear the seam open.
nodes.story: A colossal eye of ender frozen in the void. Its surface is an iris of fibers along which the endermen walk; at the pole is the pupil, a bottomless well through which the Eye looks at every world at once. Look into the rift: the pupil follows your aim. It sees you.
nodes.facts:
An eye of ender the size of a world
An iris of fibers, a pupil at the pole
It is watching

nodes.task: Make the shuttle cabin and build the shuttle on a dock of nine void plating blocks in the End, under open sky: keel, thread reel, hull, cabin, needle — the layout is below. A pearl liquefier melts ender pearls into liquid pearl: click the shuttle with a liquid pearl canister, or pipe the pearl to a launch gantry by the dock. Put a spool of rift thread into the cabin and board.
nodes.story: The shuttle is a spindle. It rises into the void on liquid pearl and passes through a rift, paying out a thread from the dock; every departure from the End takes a spool, and the way back is free: the shuttle winds itself home along the thread. Where it may go is decided by the modules in its three sockets: the Facet takes it as it is, the other worlds need glass armor, mirror boards or an eyelid, each made of what the worlds before them yield.

nodes.task: Take the shuttle through the rift of the Facet.
nodes.story: Mountains of tilted crystal faces, spires of prism glass, veins of light. The shuttle hangs on its thread here: board it again to wind back to the dock. Prism glass is needed for the glass armor and the mirror boards.

nodes.task: Beat the master of the Facet: it stands in the hall of mirrors at the bottom of the Prism Deeps, and the Facetkin elder sells a chart to it. All four tiers are locked — each with its own lock; lay a Facet core on the altar; facet golems drop it, and the elder trades one. The first sign of the fight is its colored doubles: find the real archon.
nodes.story: The First Cut built it of prism glass to keep the light in order, and when the cutters were gone it went on sorting everything that came in — light, moths, refractors, their own children. In every phase it changes: the light splits, a fan of spectrum blades opens behind it and its glass turns to opal; then it silvers into a mirror with mirror shields on its arms; at last the glass goes dark and white-gold light breaks through every seam under a crown of light. Its prism wakes the gate of the Facet, the glass armor of the shuttle is built around it, and the Staff of the First Cut sets it whole; the mirror boards are cut from the shards of its mirror shields, which it drops. Beyond the altar the treasury of the sanctum opens.

nodes.task: Make glass armor of prism glass from the Facet around the Prism Archon's prism and fit it into a socket on the shuttle hull.
nodes.story: The vapor of the Breath eats iron and purpur alike, but not the glass of the Facet: light passes through it, and acid slides off. With the armor the shuttle may enter the Breath.

nodes.task: Make mirror boards of prism glass, mirror coating and a shard of the Prism Archon's mirror shield — the archon drops it along with its prism — and fit them into a socket on the shuttle hull.
nodes.story: Shulkers guard the Hive and fire at everything that moves — except their own reflection. With mirrors on its sides the shuttle slips between the combs unseen.

nodes.task: Fit the glass armor and take the shuttle through the rift of the Breath. The vapor there is acid and there is no air: wear the full spacesuit, filled at an oxygen tank, with an Acid-Proof Coating in its torso.
nodes.story: Two tiers of lilac vapor, islands of searing glass above them, lightning between. The vapor is acid and there is no air: a suit with a coating is a must. Fulgurite from the islands is needed for the eyelid.

nodes.task: Beat the master of the Breath: it coils on the crown of the Fulgurite Spire, the Ringers' tower on an island of searing glass, and the Glassbreather elder sells a chart to it at the fourth level. All four tiers of the tower are locked — each with its own lock; lay two drake skull glasses on the altar of the crown; vapor drakes drop them. The first sign of the fight is its acid jet: hide behind the needle or a fulgurite crest.
nodes.story: The breath of the dragon that did not scatter: it drifted to the crown of the spire, where the bolts fell most often, and gathered on glass the lightning had fused into a spine. In every phase it changes: its lilac vapor sours to acid green with swollen clouds and a crop, then darkens to a thunderhead with a crown of lightning, and at last it remembers the dragon — black vapor, purple eyes and wings of vapor on fulgurite fingers. Its lung wakes the gate of the Breath, and the Wyrm's Horn is built around it; the needle door opens, and the stair inside leads up to the belfry treasury.

nodes.task: Fit the mirror boards and take the shuttle through the rift of the Hive.
nodes.story: Hexagonal combs of purpur stacked into columns and wells full of chorus wax. The wax is needed for the eyelid.

nodes.task: Beat the mistress of the Hive: she sleeps in her throne-shell at the bottom of the Wax Deeps, and the Comb Keeper elder sells a chart to them at the fourth level (his first chart leads to a ruin above). All four tiers are locked — each with its own lock; in the queen's chamber lay a warden plate on the altar; hive wardens drop it. The first sign of the fight is her bullets: strike them down or hide behind the cocoons.
nodes.story: The mother of the shell-folk: while the Comb flew, she sat in its middle and hummed. When she closed her shell, the combs went still and came down — the Settling. She changes in every phase: lilac and half-open; then sealed like a cell — amber webs between the ribs of her shell, armor of wax, honey combs below; at last she remembers the flight — the outer fan of her shell is torn away and the wax armor falls, two pairs of wings open, a crown of chorus crystals rises and a halo of cells circles her head. Her royal jelly goes into the Eyelid of the shuttle, wakes the gate of the Hive or goes whole into the Fan of the Mother; beyond the altar the royal treasury opens.

nodes.task: Make an eyelid of chorus wax from the Hive, fulgurite from the Breath and the jelly of the Mother of the Comb, and fit it into a socket on the shuttle hull.
nodes.story: The Eye sees everything that comes through its rift and turns it to glass with its gaze. Wax hides the shuttle; fulgurite grounds the gaze. With the eyelid the shuttle may enter the Eye.

nodes.task: Fit the eyelid and take the shuttle through the rift of the Eye.
nodes.story: A world that is an eye: a black pupil pit in the middle and an iris of fibers in rings around it — a golden rim and golden rays by the pupil, a pale wavy collarette, then green fibers with dark crypts and a dark limbal ring at the edge; the white sclera with its vessels beyond. Gaze crystal grows in the pupil.

nodes.task: Beat the master of the Eye: he hangs over the well of the great pupil at the bottom of the Iris Deeps, and the Lashkin elder sells a chart to them at the fourth level. All four tiers are locked — each with its own lock; lay two lens crystals, mined from the white, on the altar in the middle of the well. The first sign of the fight is his gaze: hide behind the pillars.
nodes.story: The eldest of the brothers of the Vigil did not blink for nine days, and on the tenth the Eye looked out through him. In every phase he changes: his green iris floods with amber, then the white floods with blood and his lids grow thorns, then the pupil opens and the eye within the eye looks out. Dying, he closes his eyes at last. His lens wakes the gate of the Eye, and the Vigil Dagger grows around it; beyond the altar the treasury of the Vigil opens.

nodes.task: Find a fallen meteorite and break off a piece of its crust. Meteorites fall once every few days, far from dwellings; for ten minutes a column of smoke stands over a fresh one, glowing at night, until its core is taken.
nodes.story: Under the fused crust lies iron with nickel: nine parts of iron in ten, richer than any ore on Earth. The crossed bands in the metal grow only while it cools by a degree in a million years. The hot core holds stardust; with silk touch it comes out whole — the gate of the Earth asks for one.

nodes.task: Build a fuel plant and fill a canister. Open the plant, put in coal and empty canisters. Two pieces of coal fill one canister. Hoppers work with the plant too.
nodes.story: Liquid fuel has been made from coal since the 1920s: coal is turned into gas, and the gas into kerosene. The same plant extracts helium-3 from lunar regolith — four blocks per canister — and from the haze of the gas giants. The solar wind has been bringing it to the Moon for billions of years; fusion engines run on it.

nodes.task: Charge a flat battery: a rocket does not fly without a charged one. A charging station needs no beams: set it under the open sky and put up to four flat batteries in it — in daylight it charges them one after another, half a minute each. A battery block charges them from the grid too.
nodes.story: Each rocket flight drains one battery and leaves it flat. A battery is put into the rocket through its window or simply by clicking the rocket with it in hand. The power engineers of the villages swap a flat battery and an emerald for a charged one, and a master sells the station itself.

nodes.task: Make the cabin and build the rocket on a launch pad of nine blocks, from the bottom up: the layout is below. The rocket assembles itself once its last block is in place. Open the rocket, put in fuel canisters and a charged battery: batteries are charged by a charging station in sunlight. Fit a landing module into a socket on the hull: without it only the cabin comes down. Then press Board.
nodes.story: A single stage with four fins. The tank holds ten canisters: four take you to the Moon, four bring you back — if the whole rocket lands: without a landing module only the cabin comes down, with an empty tank, and to lift off again the rocket needs a launch pad on the Moon or a return stage. Each flight drains one battery. There is no air on the Moon: board in a full spacesuit. The rocket lands where it stood before; break any part of it and it falls back into blocks.

nodes.task: Make a landing module and fit it on the rocket: click a socket on the hull with the module in hand; sneak and click the socket with an empty hand to take it off. Without it the stages burn up on the way and only the cabin comes down, with an empty tank. To lift off from another world the rocket needs a launch pad there — or a return stage in the second socket.
nodes.story: The lunar rocket has two sockets, the interplanetary three, the heavy four, the deep-space rocket six. Besides landing and return there are an extra tank (half as much fuel again), a kick stage (a fifth less fuel per flight), a battery pack, a solar array that recharges the parked rocket, life support (air in the cabin and around the landed rocket), a cargo bay of nine slots, a passenger seat and a surface scanner that points to the nearest settlement after landing. The cargo bay and the passenger seat fit the shuttle and the bell too.

nodes.task: Fly to the Moon: open the rocket, press Board and pick the Moon on the star map — the sky above the rocket must be open. Pack for the way back before you go: there is no launch pad on the Moon, so fit a return stage into the second socket; the flight drains the battery, so take a second charged one; and fuel, if the tank is not full. Put on the full spacesuit, filled at an oxygen tank: there is no air there. The lunar day scorches and the night freezes: a bare suit holds them off for a couple of minutes, a Cooling Unit or a Heating Unit in its torso — for as long as it has charge.
nodes.story: 384,400 kilometers: three days for Apollo, a few minutes for you. Gravity here is six times weaker, the sky is black even by day, and the Earth hangs above the horizon without ever setting. Moonstone and impact glass are needed for the next rocket.

nodes.task: Beat the master of the Moon: it sleeps in the Selenite Catacombs, and the Lunarian elder sells a chart to them. Bring three selenite cores — one for the deep gate, two for the altar; selenite stalkers drop them, and they come out at night. The first sign of the fight is the sweep of its arm: keep to its side.
nodes.story: It slept at the bottom of the largest crater for longer than the maria have existed, a hill of regolith and selenite. It changes in every phase: its blue crystals glow orange, then red. Its selenite heart is needed for the cabin of the interplanetary rocket and to wake the gate of the Moon, and it goes whole into the Colossus Scepter; beyond the altar the treasury opens.

nodes.task: Make the cabin of the interplanetary rocket: it needs the lunar cabin, a navigation crystal of moonstone and stardust, a heat shield of impact glass — and the heart of the Selenite Colossus, the master of the Moon: nobody leaves the Moon behind until its master is beaten. The rocket is taller and carries two boosters.
nodes.story: Boosters lift the rocket out of Earth's gravity; the heat shield lets it brake in the atmosphere of another planet. The tank holds twenty canisters — enough for Mars and back.

nodes.task: Fly to Mars. It is cold there and freezing at night: put a Heating Unit into the spacesuit torso.
nodes.story: Rust-colored deserts, dust storms that cover the whole planet, and the tallest volcano in the Solar System. Fire opal glows in the caves and dry ice lies near the poles: both are needed for a fusion engine.

nodes.task: Beat the master of Mars: it sits on the throne at the bottom of the casemates of the Rust Bastion, and the Martian elder sells a chart to them. Bring four hematite plates — one for the gate of the first level, three for the altar before the throne; canyon rollers drop them, and roller herders sell them. The first sign of the fight is a glowing crack under your feet: keep moving.
nodes.story: The king of the rust scorpions slept under the greatest dune, and the Martians say their storms were its tossing in its sleep; the garrison of the bastion dug into its bed. In every phase it changes: it shakes off the dune and its crown grows into a crimson diadem, the storm polishes it to a lilac mirror, and at last its iron core boils over — the plates go black and crack with white heat. Its hematite heart holds a field like a magnet: it goes into the cabin of the heavy rocket as the core of its fusion engine, wakes the gate of Mars or goes whole into the Tyrant's Claw; beyond the throne the treasury of the bastion opens.

nodes.task: Fly to Venus. Under its clouds of sulfuric acid it is scorching hot: without a Cooling Unit and an Acid-Proof Coating in the spacesuit torso the acid eats through you in ten seconds.
nodes.story: The hottest planet: 460 degrees under clouds of sulfuric acid. Soviet Venera probes lasted about an hour here. The mountain tops are covered with metal frost — it goes into fusion coils.

nodes.task: Beat the mistress of Venus: she squats at the bottom of the Acid Deeps under a pump tower, and the elder of the Cloud Dwellers sells a chart to them. Bring three acid glands — one for the lock of the first level, two for the altar; acid toads drop them. The first sign of the fight is her tongue shot at whoever backs away: leap aside or raise a shield.
nodes.story: The mother of every acid toad on Venus: her throat holds more acid than all the cisterns together, and when she calls, her children come. In every phase she changes: she gulps sulfur and swells yellow, with glowing blisters on her back; then her skin goes almost black, red-hot veins run through it, her acid burns orange and tusks grow from her jaw. Her caustic heart is needed for the cabin of the heavy rocket and to wake the gate of Venus, and it goes whole into the Caustic Tongue; beyond the altar the treasury of the cistern opens.

nodes.task: Make the cabin of the heavy rocket: it needs the interplanetary cabin, the caustic heart of the Acid Matriarch, the mistress of Venus, and the hematite heart of the Hematite Tyrant, the master of Mars — the core of the fusion engine. The engine itself is wound with fusion coils of fire opal and metal frost. The rocket runs on helium-3, which the fuel plant extracts from lunar regolith.
nodes.story: A fusion engine and four boosters. Mercury is closer than Mars, but lies deep in the gravity well of the Sun: braking there takes more fuel than flying to Jupiter.

nodes.task: Fly to Mercury. Its day is a furnace and its night a deep freeze: put a Cooling Unit and a Heating Unit into the spacesuit torso.
nodes.story: The Sun here is three times larger than in the Earth's sky. By day the ground heats up to 430 degrees, by night it cools to minus 180. Scorched crust and hollow salt shield a ship from radiation; golden sulfide is needed for the graviscope.

nodes.task: Beat the master of Mercury: it keeps the bottom of the Terminator Deeps, and the elder of the Terminator Folk sells a chart to them. Bring three cinder hearts — one for the heart lock of the first level, two for the altar; cinder walkers drop them, though not often. The first sign of the fight is the ground lighting up: a pillar of sunlight strikes there a moment later.
nodes.story: A knight of sulfide and salt that walks the line between the day and the night of Mercury and cannot stop: wherever it stands, noon and midnight meet. It changes in every phase: at noon the fire wins — its salt glazes gold and flames run along the helm and the blade; at midnight the ice wins — the sulfide freezes blue and an ice crown grows on the helm; in the eclipse its armor turns black and a spinning corona rises behind its head. Its core — half coal that never cools, half rime that never melts — holds the line between heat and cold, as the shielding of a reactor must: it becomes the heart of the reactor shielding of the deep-space rocket, wakes the gate of Mercury or goes whole into the Twilight Blade.

nodes.task: Fly to Jupiter. Gravity there is two and a half times that of Earth and the clouds are freezing: put an Antigravity Unit and a Heating Unit into the spacesuit torso. Ammonia crystals and red phosphorus grow inside the clouds: in the fog a vein glints like a colored star, and where it lies close to the edge of a cloud, the cloud sparkles and a pale pillar of light stands over it.
nodes.story: Jupiter has no surface: the rocket settles on the upper cloud deck. The Great Red Spot is a storm larger than the Earth that has been raging for at least three hundred years.

nodes.task: Beat the master of Jupiter: he rises to the ring in the lowest holds of the Storm Bastion, which hangs in the clouds — the Belt Rider elder sells a chart to it. The gate before the ring asks for the storm fuse hidden on that same tier, the altar for two storm glands; storm rays drop them. The first sign of the fight is his ram: step aside.
nodes.story: The last of the cloud whales: he lived in the Great Red Spot and fed on its lightning, and the Milkers built their ring to lure him. He was not evil, only enormous and hungry. In every phase he changes: full of lightning, he turns electric blue with frozen bolts on his back; then he becomes the Spot itself — scarlet, a storm tower turning on his back; at last he sinks into the Depths, black, cracked with violet and grown over with metallic hydrogen. His storm heart goes into the cabin of the deep-space rocket, wakes the gate of Jupiter or goes whole into the Leviathan's Wing; beyond the ring the treasury of the bastion opens.

nodes.task: Make the cabin of the deep space rocket: it needs the heavy cabin, the storm heart of the Spot Leviathan, the master of Jupiter, and reactor shielding from the rocks of Mercury laid around the core of the Terminator Warden, its master: one core shields the whole ship. The ship carries a habitat module and four side blocks with engines of their own.
nodes.story: The way to Neptune took Voyager 2 twelve years. The habitat ring turns to give the crew weight: without it the body forgets how to walk.

nodes.task: Fly to Saturn. Its clouds are bitterly cold: without a Heating Unit in the spacesuit torso the frost gets you within a couple of minutes. Helium pearls and tholin amber hide inside the clouds: look for a glint in the fog, sparkles and pale pillars of light over the cloud tops.
nodes.story: The rings are made of ice, from dust to blocks the size of a house, and are only tens of meters thick. At the north pole the clouds form a regular hexagon: each of its sides is longer than the Earth is wide.

nodes.task: Beat the master of Saturn: he waits under the lower dome of the Ring Observatory, which hangs in the clouds below the rings — the Ring Keeper elder sells a chart to it. The gate before the dome asks for the Watcher's ocular hidden on that same tier, the altar for two tufts of glider fluff; ring gliders drop them. The first sign of the fight is his fan of shards: step aside.
nodes.story: The storm at the north pole of Saturn keeps six corners because it has a master: a heart of ice wearing six rings of the Crown that never reached a net — the Ring Keepers call him the Six-Crowned. When the Watchers turned their great lens on the pole, he came down to see who was looking. In every phase he changes: the turquoise winter hexagon turns to golden summer haze and his halo shatters; then the aurora — all lilac, a cloud hexagon of the storm rises around his belt; at last the heat of the depths — the ice goes dark, crimson fire shines through the cracks and a crown of spikes grows. His hexagon core wakes the gate of Saturn or goes whole into the Six-Crowned Pernach; beyond the dome the treasury of the observatory opens.

nodes.task: Fly to Uranus. Its air is the coldest in the Solar System: take a Heating Unit in the spacesuit torso. Diamond hail and methane clathrate hide inside the clouds: look for a glint in the fog and a pillar of light over a cloud, and listen: near a vein the crystals chime.
nodes.story: Uranus lies on its side: its axis points almost at the Sun, and a polar day lasts forty-two years. Methane ice drifts among its clouds.

nodes.task: Beat the master of Uranus: he rose out of the hail in the throne hall of the Frost Citadel, frozen into a berg above the clouds — the Frostwalker elder sells a chart to it. The gate before the hall asks for the first hailstone hidden on that same tier, the altar before the throne for two diamond splinters; diamond crabs drop them. The first sign of the fight is his fan of hail: step between the stones.
nodes.story: The hail the expedition heaped in its throne hall stood up in the Long Night as a king of methane ice. The Frostwalkers call him the Gatherer: he gathers the hail into himself, and so he grows, and the warmth out of everything near him, and so the lamps go cold. In every phase he changes: hydrogen tints his hail lilac and druses grow on his shoulders; then the diamond lattice shifts and he blushes pink under a high crown; in the Long Night his ice goes black, and the stolen warmth glows amber through his broken window. His Cryo Heart wakes the gate of Uranus or goes whole into the Gatherer's Flail; beyond the throne the treasury of the citadel opens.

nodes.task: Fly to Neptune. Its clouds are as cold as those of Uranus: take a Heating Unit in the spacesuit torso. Black diamonds and superionic ice hide inside the clouds: through the fog they glint like violet and blue stars.
nodes.story: The fastest winds in the Solar System: two thousand kilometers per hour. The Sun from here is just a very bright star, and its light takes four hours to arrive.

nodes.task: Beat the master of Neptune: the Locked Wind coils on the bridge of the Abyss Vault, a Hanging House whose mast sticks up above the white cloud; the Windbearer elder sells a chart to it. The bulkhead before the bridge asks for the ballast key hidden on that same deck, the altar for two maw lures; the maws of the Dark Spot drop them. The first sign of the fight is his rush: step off his line.
nodes.story: The fastest wind in the Solar System went into the Hanging House through the broken windows and could not find the way out: it forgot its words, grew scales of black diamond from the vault's rain and only screamed. In every phase it changes: first black and blue, with the rim of a porthole on its neck; then lilac, with lightning in its veins and a druse of black diamonds along its back; then the rim bursts, the plates are torn away and white wind blows through the cracks. You did not kill it — you let it go. Its heart, a knot of wind in a cracked black diamond, wakes the gate of Neptune or goes whole into the Tail of the Gale; beyond the bridge the treasury of the vault opens.

nodes.task: Talk to the natives of another world: the Lunarians live on the Moon, in the Lunar Court on the dark plains of the maria — round stone domes half sunk in the regolith, a mirror bowl with the blue reflection of the Earth, lamps of moonstone. Click one of them: the talkative ones answer, the rest show their wares at once, unless they have a task for you. Answers are chosen with the mouse or keys 1–9. A rocket with a surface scanner names the nearest settlement as soon as it lands.
nodes.story: Each of the sixteen worlds reached by rocket, shuttle or bell has its own people: the Martians build tall red towers with windcatchers, the Belt Riders hover over the clouds of Jupiter and never touch the ground, the Comb Keepers slam their lids and hide when struck, the Fruiting Folk are fruit of the Mycelium itself. They remember who you are: what you have asked, what they have given you, which master you have beaten. Ask a Frostwalker about the crystals on its back, and it will give you a diamond: to them it is only weather. Every elder sells a chart to the dungeon of their world, and most of them later sell what its gate or altar asks for. They trade like villagers, for emeralds and the currency of their world, and the stock is renewed every day.

nodes.task: Take a task from a native and hand it in. A golden "!" over a head means the native has a task for you: talk to them — a talkative one shows the task line above the answers (the Q key), the others speak of the task at once. A gray "?" means the task is taken but not done yet; a golden "?" means everything is done: come back for the reward. Taken tasks are in the task window: the F7 key, the scroll button in the inventory or the Tasks tab of this journal; one of them can be tracked in the corner of the screen. The first task of the Lunarian elder is Our First Home: go down into the Selenite Catacombs.
nodes.story: Every people has fourteen to sixteen tasks shared among its crafts: bring what their world lacks, defeat the creatures that trouble them, find the places of their stories, live through the events of their world, defeat its master, carry a parcel to another craft or another people. Tasks open one another, like a story: the Lunarian Earth Keeper sends two moonstones to the Martian elder, and a Martian storm warden answers with a fire opal for the Moon. The reward is emeralds and the currency of the world, things of the world, experience — and sometimes a secret, a discount or wares sold to no one else: defeat the master of their world for the elder, and every trader of that people gives you a tenth off. A blue "!" is a task that can be taken again every day: a Cloud Dweller condenser keeper takes two buckets of Earth water every day.

nodes.task: Find a structure of another world. Every world has seven to ten of them, and they stand in plain sight: on the Moon a Fallen Lander with its hatch still open, a black Monolith in a paved crater, a Relay Mast whose beacon still blinks.
nodes.story: Further out they grow stranger: in the Ash the Giant's Skull, thirty blocks across, with one eye socket burning blue; in the Forge the Slag Lighthouse, with living gold burning in its cage; in the Lament the Weeping Statue, crying into a pool that never fills. Every such place keeps a chest or a barrel with a page of this journal about it and the loot of that world — upgrade cards, suit units, craft modules. Settlements, gates, dungeons and the giant mushrooms of the Mycelium count too.

nodes.task: Enter the dungeon of another world. Every world has one, several tiers deep, and its entrance stands in the open: on the Moon it is a shrine of eight columns over a shaft that leads down into the Selenite Catacombs; on the giants the whole dungeon rises among the clouds, in the Breath it is a tower on an island of glass. The elder of the world's people sells a chart to it — on the Moon, the Lunarian elder.
nodes.story: Sealed doorways crumble when their puzzle is solved. A keystone socket takes one thing of its world — the deep gate of the catacombs wants the selenite core of a selenite stalker; rune plates are walked in the order of the signs on the wall, and a wrong step puts out every lit plate; a beam must reach its receiver — click a mirror to turn it. Every chest keeps a book with the story of the place, and in the Giant's Ossuary or the Tear Deeps the lecterns still hold the notes of those who lived there. Deep inside stands the altar of the master: click it and it tells you what offering it awaits. Beyond it lies the treasury — the ore of the world, and sometimes its gear: the Prism Blade in the Prism Deeps, the Gilded Heart in the Gilded Deeps.

nodes.task: Defeat the guardian of a lair. Some ruins are not empty: on the Moon a sphinx of mare basalt lies before the sealed portal of the Dust Tomb, in the Forge a salamander sleeps coiled by the pool of gold in its den. A guardian sleeps until you come close — then it wakes, and its bar lights up. It does not leave its lair: go far enough and it returns, lies down and heals. Its seals keep the treasure of the lair shut while it lives.
nodes.story: When a guardian falls, the seals of its lair crumble. It leaves a trophy no other creature has — the mask of the sphinx, the gill of the salamander — and a trophy makes an item of its world: the Sphinx Mask becomes the Ring of the Sleepless Warden, the Fire Gill the Firegill Belt. Every world has one or two guardians, and each ruin keeps its own: a guardian once beaten does not come back.

nodes.task: Wake a world gate. A ring of gate frames stands on Earth and in each of the sixteen worlds: nine by nine without corners, the gate heart at the bottom. Click the heart with an empty hand to see what it awaits. The ring of the Moon answers one who has beaten the Selenite Colossus and lived through a meteor shower there, and asks for the Selenite Heart, 48 stardust, 8 titanium ingots and 6 selenite shards — all at once: click the heart holding any of them.
nodes.story: Awakened gates are joined: click the heart, pick a gate, and you stand before its ring. A passage costs four supplies of the world you leave — stardust from the planets, void shards from the worlds beyond the rifts, deep embers from the worlds below the vents; during a parade of planets it is free. Supplies come from the telescopes — shooting stars, cracks in the sky of the End, fire bubbles in the magma — and from the events of the worlds. The End and the Nether have no ring of their own: build one — four gate frames from obsidian, hull plates and stardust, and a gate heart from frames, resonance rings and a gravity core. In the End it wakes once the dragon is slain and every rift torn open, in the Nether once the Wither is slain and every vent heard. A finished ring cannot be broken; an unfinished one you take apart yourself — sneak and click with an empty hand.

nodes.task: Make a shipyard console from the heart of the master who ends the first worlds of a road — the Terminator Warden of Mercury, the Mother of the Comb of the Hive or the Giant's Remnant of the Ash — and set it at the middle of a long side of a slipway of nine by five plates, with two crane towers of four sections at opposite corners. Click the console: it shows with lights what is still missing.
nodes.story: A complete shipyard lights up and becomes one great machine: cranes over the slipway, guide lights along its edges, a hologram of a ship over the console. It builds ships whose blueprints you know — the scout of a road is known after that master, the hauler after the last master of the road; the rest are drawn on blueprints from space caches and stations — and raises a ship on the slipway to the next class. It also takes a ship apart: hold the Take apart button, and its modules, hold, cockpit, core and part of its hull sections and drives go to the shipyard store; fuel drains into empty buckets and canisters from your inventory.

nodes.task: Build the shipyard: the console at the middle of a long side of a slipway of nine by five plates, two crane towers of four sections at opposite corners (the scheme and its Show in the world button are on the Shipyard page). Click the console and pick a form: the slipway takes hull sections, drives, a cockpit and a ship core from your inventory, and the cranes put it together part by part. A ship leaves the slipway with an empty tank: fill it with the fuel of its road.
nodes.story: A ship flies over a world like a plane and leaves the sky for open space. Lift-off and boost burn fuel; cruising is free. Rocks and crashes wear the hull — the metals of the road mend it, and a hull section raises a wreck. Its hold stays with the ship wherever it is, and a ship beacon tuned to it calls it to you — at once within a world, and from another world or deep space not at once and not for free: fuel for the trip, or a tug for the supply of the road.

nodes.task: Fuel the ship, sit in the cockpit and climb: W is thrust, Space lifts, Ctrl is boost. Keep climbing — the top right of the instruments counts the blocks left to space. Where the sky ends, the shutter closes, and the ship comes out into the open space of its road.
nodes.story: Open space is a world of its own: the worlds of the road hang in it as globes, and between them lies what is found nowhere else. The instruments name the target under the crosshair, its distance and the time to it. In space the ship coasts: let go of the keys and it keeps its course. Cruising is free — a ship with an empty tank still flies, only without boost and jumps. The first target is the Moon: aim at it and fly.

nodes.task: Enter the sky of a world from space: aim the crosshair at its globe and fly until the shutter closes. The ship comes out high above the ground — hold Shift to descend, and on the ground press Shift again to step out. A ship lands only where you have already landed by rocket, shuttle or bell; the Moon is the nearest.
nodes.story: The globe keeps the spot the ship took off from: the Launch Site mark leads back to your pad. Lift-off burns fuel by the gravity of the world — a quarter of a bucket on Earth, a sixth of that on the Moon, more than half a bucket on Jupiter: look at the tank before you land on a heavy world. Click the nose of a standing ship to sit in the cockpit, its stern to go aboard.

nodes.task: In space aim the crosshair at a body or a station and press the autopilot key (the full stop by default): the ship flies there by itself. Then press the Go aboard key (the semicolon by default) and walk about your ship while it flies.
nodes.story: Every ship has a deck. The pilot seat takes you back to the cockpit, the hold chest is the hold of the ship, the chart table shows the course, the rack holds the modules, and the bunk shortens a long flight: sleep, and the ship is there. Any thrust key takes the helm back from the autopilot. On the ground the stern hatch lets you out; in space it opens only when the ship stands on a pad. Without a target the autopilot simply holds the course of the nose.

nodes.task: Fly your ship to a station of a people: each hangs near its world, on the sunward side. A ship scanner pulse marks a station from far away; closer, it is a blinking light, then a silhouette.
nodes.story: Six peoples of the Solar System keep a station in open space: the Stillwatch of the Lunarians by the Moon, Fear's Nest of the Martians inside Phobos, the Ark Bubble of the Cloud Dwellers over Venus, the Io Mast of the Belt Riders by Jupiter, the Crown Station of the Ring Keepers in the rings of Saturn and the Triton Anchor of the Windbearers by Neptune. Land on the pad: the dock console refuels and repairs the ship for stardust and raises its class for the same price as a shipyard. Inside there is air. A station you have visited becomes a jump target.

nodes.task: Aim the crosshair at a body farther than 1,500 blocks and hold the jump key (the grave accent by default, under Esc) for a second and a half. A jump burns a bucket of fuel for every 20,000 blocks.
nodes.story: A jump lasts four seconds whatever the distance and brings the ship out two radii from the target, still heading for it at cruising speed: brake (S) or turn away unless you mean to enter its sky. A scout jumps 40 thousand blocks at a time, an explorer a hundred thousand; a jump drive module adds half again and saves fuel. Far scanner marks — fields, caches, wrecks, stations you have visited, anomalies you have noticed — are jump targets too. A scout does not reach Neptune on one tank: refuel at the stations on the way, carry canisters in the hold, or cruise for free.

nodes.task: Bring back an ore that no world has. In the Solar System fly out past Mars to the Main Belt and press the scanner key (the comma by default): the pulse marks fields and rich rocks. Mine a nickel-iron asteroid — with a pickaxe in a spacesuit, or from the cockpit with a mining beam module (hold the beam key, Left Alt by default).
nodes.story: Tetrataenite sits in the nickel-iron of the Main Belt, osmiridium in the red Trojans by Jupiter, pallasite olivine in rare pallasites. The islands of the Interrift keep condensed void and chorus quartz, the Depths ringwoodite and the fire rose of magma geodes. This matter pays for ship classes, tier II modules and the orbital emitter, and station folk buy it. In a field the ship flies by the chart — no faster than the terrain arrives. Fields hide caches of old expeditions: every second one keeps a blueprint.

nodes.task: Make a ship module and fit it in the ship console (E in the cockpit or sneak-click). A class C ship has two or three sockets; every class adds one.
nodes.story: Eleven modules in three tiers: drive, thrusters, armor, cargo pods, scanner, tank, jump drive, mining beam, regolith processor, heat shield and corona scoop. Tier I comes from the metals of the road, tier II from the ores of the belts, tier III from rare finds of open space. The mining beam cuts whatever the pilot looks at (hold the beam key, Left Alt by default) straight into the hold.

nodes.task: Finish an errand for the keeper of a station — the craft that lives only there: the orbit watcher, the Fear driller, the ark keeper, the flux tapper, the crown tender or the cargo master.
nodes.story: Station folk trade what a pilot needs — fuel, hull plates, ship modules — and buy the ores of the belts, ice and water. Their errands lead out into open space: ore from the belt, a parcel to the next station, a comet to catch up with, a wrecked ship to scan, a ship class to raise at a dock. The last errand of each station gives the key to its vault.

nodes.task: Raise your ship to class B. Stand it on the slipway of a shipyard or on the pad of a station dock, sound and with a full tank, and pay 64 of the supply of its road and 8 of the matter of its belts — tetrataenite ingots for a starship.
nodes.story: Each class adds 12% to speed, a quarter to hull, hold and jump range, and one module socket. Class A asks for 128 supply and two rarer kinds of belt matter; class S asks for the heart of any master of the road and the rarest thing in its space: for a starship, the core of a comet.

nodes.task: Find the wreck of an old ship: wrecks hang in the belts and on the night side of every planet and the Moon. A scanner pulse closer than 420 blocks tells you what ship it was.
nodes.story: Each wreck is a ship of a known form with its own story — the log in its chest tells it. In the wreck of a scout the ship core still glows: click it with two hull sections and a ship drive in your inventory, and the ship is yours, with its blueprint. The chests may hold blueprints of the explorer and the fighter.

nodes.task: Open the vault of any station with its key. A vault opens once for each player.
nodes.story: Every station keeps one sealed room: the Vault of Phases, the Deep Store, the Seed Bubble, the Jar Room, the Rim Treasury, the Chain Locker. Inside lie tier III ship modules, the metals of the belts, and, with the Lunarians and the Ring Keepers, the blueprints of their own ships, the Lens and the Crown Sail.

nodes.task: Catch up with a comet. One comes every two to four days for twenty minutes: the event banner announces it, and from Earth it is seen at dusk. In space aim at its mark and jump, then come closer than 64 blocks to the nucleus.
nodes.story: Near the nucleus the ship keeps pace with it by itself. The mining beam cuts crust and ice; deep in the larger lobe lies the heart — the comet core that class S asks for. On the sunlit side vents wake: the instruments warn a moment before a jet strikes. Comet ice is the richest feed for the regolith processor.

nodes.task: Notice a sky anomaly from space: the corona of the Sun, a coronal mass ejection, a gamma-ray burst, merging black holes, the light of a supernova — or the dark thing beyond the Kuiper Belt. A noticed anomaly gets a page in the codex (the Anomalies tab of this journal) and becomes a jump target.
nodes.story: Every anomaly lets you do something, not just look: scoop fuel from the corona, hide from a burst behind a planet, jump for free on the crest of a gravitational wave, ride the light of a supernova to its remnant and mine r-process ore there. Scanner pulses from different sides are data: five of them, and the anomaly is studied. The codex says how each step is done and what it gives. Some anomalies are first found from the ground: a reflector shows the Visitor creeping among the stars, an astrograph the star that flares in front of the Wanderer, a graviscope the ring of a wormhole, the smeared stars of the dark matter cloud and the chirp of merging black holes. Track a passing one and the almanac of the codex names its hour.

nodes.task: Fly to Planet Nine — the black hole beyond the Kuiper Belt, 230 thousand blocks from the Sun: once you have noticed it, jump to its mark. By the hole the instruments count twelve steps and say how to do the next three. Do not fly straight at it: a ship coasts in space, the hole pulls, and from five hundred blocks the horizon is seconds away — come in at an angle and keep S ready.
nodes.story: Swing past it for a burst of speed. Drop cargo into the ergosphere: the hole pays back in fuel and squeezes coal into diamonds. Catch Hawking sparks at the flares of the disk. Feed it full and ride its jet for forty thousand blocks. Look through it as through a lens from four focal points. Surf the gates over the disk. With a Hawking spark aboard you may dive past the horizon and come back; without one nobody returns: the instruments count the seconds to the horizon — yellow from twelve, red from six.

nodes.task: The anomaly codex gives the blueprint once three anomalies are entered. Craft the receiver, stand it on a mast of three lattice blocks and lay a dish of 48 panels around it, 7 × 7, at its level: missing blocks show as ghosts. It works on Earth, on the Moon and in orbit, by day and in rain — but keep it away from working machines: they jam it.
nodes.story: The dish does not look — it listens: above is a radio map of the whole sky, below is the waterfall, frequency across and time down. Click the map and the dish turns there. A thunderstorm and machines within 24 blocks are interference: the fewer of them, the faster a signal gathers.

nodes.task: Find a signal. Each is tuned with its own tool: a thin trace at the hydrogen line is held in the sight for 72 seconds (it comes from Sagittarius, just below the Galactic Center, once a sidereal day); the arc of a burst is straightened with the wheel; the dotted beat of a pulsar is folded until it stands as a column (try the Crab Nebula); a comb of lines is dragged onto the faint lines of a point high in Virgo. The beam panel says what it hears; a step of help costs stardust.
nodes.story: Every find is a page of the anomaly codex, stardust and a deed: pulsars make ship jumps cheaper, a burst charges batteries, the quasar gives its light to the spectral laboratory, and "Wow!" gives a bearing — not to Sagittarius, but beyond Neptune. Some sources never rise over the Earth: take a telescope to the Moon or to orbit.

nodes.task: Time all three pulsars by folding: the Crab (33 ms), PSR B1919+21 in Vulpecula (1.337 s) — and the Vela pulsar (89 ms), which a telescope sees only from the Moon or from orbit.
nodes.story: Three clocks that never drift: by them a ship knows where it is to the block. Every jump of yours now costs a quarter less fuel, and the telescope has built the device itself — the Pulsar Navigator, the heart of Interstellar Drive II. Real ships are learning the same: SEXTANT steered the space station by pulsars in 2018.

nodes.task: Meet a living flock in open space: fly up to it or catch it with a pulse of the ship scanner. From far away a flock is a handful of twinkling lights against the stars.
nodes.story: The void is not empty. Over the fields of the Main Belt and the Trojans dust rays glide in a wedge: they part before the bow and fly at the wing of a ship while it keeps to their pace. In the glare near Mercury and Venus sail moths open their mirror sails to the Sun and turn like a golden wheel. In the Kuiper Belt ice jellies drift: come close, and one flares up and strikes with a wave of cold — the hull ices over, the glass of the cabin frosts. And in the nickel-iron of the asteroids rockgnawers sleep: cut into their rock with a pickaxe or the mining beam, and one bursts out and bites — or clings to the hull until full speed shakes it off. Each leaves something of use: the sieve of a ray makes filters and sifts stardust, a tooth melts into tetrataenite, a stinger lines a hull against the cold, sail foil makes solar cells.

nodes.task: Make a pulse cannon, fit it in the ship console — into a weapon hardpoint, or into a module socket if the ship has no hardpoints — take off and fire: the attack button is the trigger while the ship flies.
nodes.story: A pulse cannon fires a beam, not a shell: the pulse lands where the diamond mark of the sight is, in the same instant, at up to 96 blocks. Six pulses a second; three seconds of fire overheat the barrels, and they stay silent for two — watch the arc under the sight. A target close to the sight is framed; when the frame closes and turns red, the pulses will land. Fighters carry two cannons, and they fire in turn. A pulse hurts the creatures of open space and cracks drifting boulders — a shard flies off now and then, and the ship picks it up by flying through it — but it is no mining beam: it wastes most of the rock. Each pulse burns a little fuel.

nodes.task: Fight off a swarm of rockgnawers: shoot one down with the cannon or shake one off the hull at speed. A swarm finds a ship that idles in a field of the Main Belt or in a cluster.
nodes.story: Rockgnawers feed on nickel-iron, and a hull is nickel-iron too. Three to five burst out of a boulder nearby, catch up and settle on the bow, the wings and the back — each gnaws a point of hull a second. The panel on the left counts the hunters and those already on the hull; red arrows point at them. While they hunt, the ship flies at combat speed: no faster than its cruise, with boost only in short bursts — the bar shows the charge. Full speed for a second and a half shakes them off; the one on the bow sits right in the sight. A shaken gnawer comes back; a dead one leaves a tooth. In the open void a ship outruns the swarm; among the rocks it cannot.

nodes.task: Kill the Belt Devourer from your ship — a worm the size of an asteroid that eats out the fields of the Main Belt.
nodes.story: The belt really has gaps — the Kirkwood gaps, swept clean by the pull of Jupiter (Daniel Kirkwood, 1866). The peoples say otherwise: these are the trails of the Devourer. It feeds in one field of the Main Belt, and it is found by its trail: the ship scanner marks eaten-out fields — from old cold furrows to fresh ones, and at the end the worm itself. Its plates of meteoric iron turn shots aside. It is hurt in two places only: the link that glows while a swallowed boulder goes down its body, and the open throat. It rams — leave the line, up and sideways. It spits rubble — and then eats that rubble, and every boulder is another glowing lump. Below two thirds of its health its heat turns amber and it breathes in: the stream drags ships and rocks into the millstones — thrust out of it, or stay and fire down the throat until it chokes. Below one third it burns white, goes dark and dives into the field: a ring of rubble shows where it will come up — do not be there; after it surfaces two lumps go down its body at once. A wrecked ship is mended and flown back — its wounds do not heal. Inside it are osmiridium and pallasite olivine, and the Millstone Heart: every pilot who hit its soft places gets a share. Eight days later another comes along the old trails.

nodes.task: Shoot down a drifter ship. They wait for an armed ship by the asteroid belts and on the lanes between stations — never near a station itself.
nodes.story: Drifters are outcasts of every people, and their ships are sewn from wrecks: a Shell is a cockpit, one wing and two odd engines; a Patcher is a gunboat in patches of every color; a Tug hauls crates. An ambush comes at once, two or three ships; a raid of three to five is announced by the instruments twenty seconds ahead — time to run to a station or to turn and meet it. They close in, then circle the ship at forty blocks or so, broadside on, and fire in bursts: a ship that flies across their line of fire is hard to hit, a ship that sits still is not. The frame shows the hull of the target; at a quarter of it the ship breaks off and runs with what it has. A downed ship falls apart: its plating drifts as scrap for the mining beam, and your share of the spoils lies in the wreckage — fly through the gold mark to take it. Each pilot who fought gets a share of their own.

nodes.task: Sack the lair of the drifters on Deimos, the outer moon of Mars: shoot down its turrets and every guard ship.
nodes.story: Free Haven is where the raids of the Solar System come from — they always arrive from its side. The haven trades with no one and docks no one: a ship that comes within a hundred and fifty blocks wakes three turrets and the guard, and there are never more than six enemies at once — as one falls, the next leaves the lair, until the garrison of eight ships runs out. The guards of the lair do not run at a quarter of the hull: they have nowhere to go. Retreat, and those still alive go back inside; what you shot down stays shot down. When the last one falls, the stores are open — every pilot who fought gets a share at the haven: tallies, torpedo packs, tetrataenite, plating, and now and then a module. For three days no raids come in the Solar System; then the lair is rebuilt.

nodes.task: Disable a drifter ship instead of wrecking it: shoot out its engines with the pulse cannon.
nodes.story: A drifter ship can be taken whole. Its engines are the glowing cells in the tail; the target frame marks them with a small square and shows their reserve as a second, orange bar under the hull. Get behind the ship or beside it and put the pulses there: when the reserve is gone, the ship loses way, the crew leaves in an escape pod, and the hull stays adrift — disabled and empty. Shots that land elsewhere go into the hull, and a hull at zero falls apart as before; the mass driver and the torpedoes always go into the hull — brute force leaves no trophy. Your share of the spoils lies by the hull either way. A disabled hull waits for six minutes: take it into the hold with the beam and bring it home — a shipyard can strip it for parts or refit it into a ship of your own. Guards of the lair and the Ark cannot be taken.

nodes.task: Cross from one ship to another through a light sleeve: look at a ship within 16 blocks and press the Go aboard key.
nodes.story: A wrecked ship does not fly, but a friend can come alongside. Match speeds (the sleeve breaks above 6 blocks a second), look at the other ship from the cockpit and press the Go aboard key: its pilot gets a request — or none, if you are a friend of that ship or its owner. A sleeve of light runs between the hatches and carries you across in a breath: to a free seat, or onto the deck if the seats are taken. From the deck the hatch does the same in open space. A pilot can also hold the capture beam on someone drifting outside — with their consent they are pulled to the hatch.

nodes.task: Take an empty wrecked ship — or a disabled drifter hull — into your hold: hold the beam key on it for six seconds.
nodes.story: The capture beam is the same key as the mining beam and needs no module. Frame a ship closer than 24 blocks and hold the key: a cocoon of light closes around it and the ship folds into your hold. It keeps everything — class, modules, fuel, hull, its own hold and its owner — and takes slots in your hold: a scout six, a hauler sixteen. One ship per carrier, two in a hauler; each costs a seventh of your speed and half as much again in jump fuel (a hauler carries it twice as lightly). Your own ship, always; another player's wrecked ship, with its owner's yes (friends of the ship need none), unless the server rules otherwise. Unload it alongside from the hold window; its owner can always call it home with the beacon.

nodes.task: Take a ship in tow: the same capture gives a tow line when people are aboard or the hold has no room.
nodes.story: People aboard stay aboard: the ship hangs 12 to 16 blocks behind on a braided line of light, and they walk its deck or look out of the cockpit. Everyone aboard is asked first — a manned ship is never towed against its will. With a line the carrier flies without boost and a jump costs twice the fuel, but the towed ship jumps with it, crosses the sky and is set down beside the carrier when it lands on the ground or a station pad. Either side lets go with the beam key.

nodes.task: Make the flagship of the drifters surrender: shoot down its four turrets, then break the hull of the Ark itself.
nodes.story: The Ark is sewn from ships of every people: the nose of a star hauler, a wing of the rift, engines of the vents, and patches over all of it. Every few days it stands for a day at the Trojans of Jupiter — the instruments announce it and show a red mark; after the lair on Deimos is sacked it comes sooner. While a single turret lives the core is sealed: shots at the hull do nothing. Each turret fires only into its own half of the sky — two look up, one to each side, none down or astern, so there is always a blind side to come from. The two engines astern are weak spots: without them the Ark stops turning. Shells leave the hangar under its belly, two at a time. The main gun in the nose charges for five seconds: a line of light shows where it will strike, and a second before the shot the line freezes — leave it, or hide behind wreckage or behind the Ark itself. With the turrets down the core is open. The Ark does not explode: it surrenders, the captain comes on the channel, and the stores are open to every pilot who fought — the Ark Core among them. In a minute the Ark is gone.

nodes.task: Make a boarding hook around the Ark Core and hold it in your hand.
nodes.story: The outcasts boarded every ship they robbed with grapples; the captain's own hook carries the reactor of the Ark in its winch drum. Throw it where you look: it bites into a wall, a drifting rock or a hull, and the drum hauls you there — in the belt you can hop from rock to rock on foot, and on a moving body you hang on the chain and fly with it. A foe is yanked to you; if it is too heavy to move, you are yanked to it.

nodes.task: Make the Millstone around the Millstone Heart of the Belt Devourer and hold it in your hand.
nodes.story: The heart of the worm is a disc of meteoric iron that never stopped turning. Strike the ground with it, and a ring of millstones rolls out, crushes everyone in its way and grinds back to where you struck. While the stones roll you are rooted to the spot — choose the moment.

nodes.task: Fire a mass driver or launch a salvo of torpedoes. Both go into the weapon hardpoints; a shield module takes the blows meanwhile.
nodes.story: A mass driver throws a slug once every second and a half while the trigger is held: sixteen damage or so, a reach of 160 blocks, and it goes through everything in line — two ships, a creature and the boulder behind it. A torpedo rack fires on the use button at the target in the frame: two to four homing torpedoes, thirty damage each, and a salvo burns one torpedo pack from the hold or from your pockets. The rack is drifter work: it takes one of their tallies to build. A shield module is not a weapon and goes into a module socket: thirty to sixty points that take the blows before the hull does; three quiet seconds, and it builds up again, four points a second. Rockgnawers gnaw under the shield.

nodes.task: Fire a void lance or slag flak — or lure an enemy torpedo away with flares.
nodes.story: Each road arms its ships in its own way.
