A void ship carries the void lance: a crack of emptiness that strikes once a second and goes straight through shields — the drifters of the Interrift wear void fields that eat pulses, and the lance does not notice them. A depth ship carries slag flak: a heavy shell with a proximity fuse that bursts by its target and burns everything within three blocks — a swarm, a cluster of fire bubbles, ships in a line, a torpedo in flight. Flares fit any ship: tugs and the Ark launch homing torpedoes, and a torpedo turns slower than you but runs faster; the swap-hands key throws a fan of burning decoys behind you, and the torpedo goes for them. Shoot down the carrier, and its torpedoes go blind.

nodes.task: Fly to the Main Belt and aim at Ceres — a dim dwarf between Mars and Jupiter. The bright spot on its globe is the salt of Occator crater: aim the crosshair right at it and you will enter the sky above the crater. Land and step out. No air, cold, a gravity of six hundredths: the suit needs a Heating Unit; jump carefully.
nodes.story: Salt and silence. The white spots are natron — soda left by brine that climbed from below; break the salt of Occator or dig natron ore from the clay rock. Natron is a flux: two raw pieces of a star metal and a pinch of it give three ingots. The salt glows at night — those are the lights of Occator; at dawn the crater breathes: brine bursts into hoar, a rainbow halo rings the Sun, and pinches of natron settle on the ground — pick them up. Young craters lie in pale rays. To the south-east stands Ahuna Mons, a lone mountain of salty ice. A day here is nine hours; the small world closes on itself.

nodes.task: Fly to Jupiter and aim at Europa, the white moon scratched with brown lines. Land on the ice and step out; the cold is deadly: the suit needs a Heating Unit. There is an ocean under the shell: look for an open crack — a dark slit of water between two ridges or between the plates of chaos — and dive. You will need air under water: a full suit tank will do.
nodes.story: A shell of ice thirty blocks thick over a sea sixty deep. Under the ice only the living glows: algae on the underside of the shell, mats around the black smokers, and the whales. The seabed is serpentinite — the crusher wrings hydrogen cells out of it; the chimneys of the smokers give copper and gold. Geysers at the edges of the cracks erupt every half a minute and throw whoever stands on them. Jupiter hangs in the north and never sets; at noon the Sun goes behind it — the world dims under a ring of fire — and at midnight it is full. The whale is curious: wait by open water and it will pass beneath you; from the ice you can see its light through the shell.

nodes.task: Fly to Jupiter and aim at Io, the yellow moon freckled with black. Before you land, fit a Suit Radiation Screen into the suit: Jupiter pours radiation onto Io, and without the screen the dose climbs in a minute — then only a roof or the cabin saves you. Take a Heating Unit for the plains; by the lava lakes it is the other way round. Land and step out.
nodes.story: The most volcanic body in the Solar System: Jupiter kneads Io with its tides, and the heat comes out through four hundred volcanoes. The plains are sulfur — yellow, red where it is fresh, white with frost. The pits called paterae hold lakes of lava under plates of dark crust: walk the plates, jump the glowing seams. Plumes stand over the great volcanoes hundreds of blocks high. In the black basalt lies peleite, glass that keeps heat: thermal modules are made of it. In the north lies Loki Patera with an island in its lake. Jupiter hangs in the north and never sets; at midnight the shadow of Io crawls across it.

nodes.task: Fly to Saturn and aim at Titan, the orange moon wrapped in haze. The air is dense but not for breathing, and the cold is deadly: you need a Heating Unit. Land and step out. Look for the dark seas near the pole.
nodes.story: The only moon with an atmosphere, and the only world besides Earth with seas — but the seas are liquid methane, and the rock is water ice. Rivers have cut canyons down to the seas; along the equator lie dunes of dark organic sand. The pale crust on the shores is evaporite: break it for benzene co-crystal; baked in a furnace it becomes polymer sheet — skin for hulls and for the Titan Wings. With them a person flies here: the air is four times denser than on Earth, and the gravity is a seventh. Methane rain falls in slow heavy drops. Saturn is a pale ghost in the haze. In the northern sea of Kraken there is an island with a tower.

nodes.task: Io lies inside the radiation belts of Jupiter. Build a Suit Radiation Screen — lead from Venus around hydrogen cells from Europa — and fit it into the suit torso at a suit rack. It needs no charge.
nodes.story: Without the screen the dose under the open sky of Io climbs to deadly in two minutes in a suit, and in one without. A roof, a sealed room or the cabin of the ship lets it fall. The counter in the helmet crackles while the dose builds. The screen takes a socket: with a tank, a cell and a Heating Unit the torso is full. Peleite from the basalt of Io makes a Thermal Module — Cooling Unit and Heating Unit in one socket — if you have read its spectrum.

nodes.task: Break the pale evaporite of the shores for benzene co-crystal, bake it into polymer sheets and stretch them on a titanium frame. Wear the wings in the chest slot, over the suit; jump, press Space in the air to spread them — and Space again to beat.
nodes.story: On Titan a person flies on muscle alone: the air is four times denser than on Earth, the gravity a seventh. Each beat costs a little hunger; the wings wear like elytra and are patched with a polymer sheet held in the other hand. In thin air they stay folded: everywhere else only elytra fly.

nodes.task: Fly to Saturn and aim at Enceladus — a tiny dazzling-white moon just outside the rings. A fan of light stands over one side of its globe: the jets of the tiger stripes. Aim at the blue lines and you will enter the sky above them; you can fly right through the fan — ice will crust the canopy. Land and step out. Deadly cold: the suit needs a Heating Unit. Gravity is six hundredths: jump carefully.
nodes.story: The whitest world in the Solar System: its snow falls from its own geysers. In the southern basin four fissures run side by side — the tiger stripes, warm blue ice that glows at night. Jets beat from their floors in a wall a quarter of a kilometer high, and a wave runs along it; a jet throws whoever steps on it sixty blocks up. In the ice by the stripes lie greenish nests of phosphate rime. Use phosphate salt on a hydroponic bed: the crop on it grows twice as fast until the salt is spent. Geyser hoppers ride the jets and glide down. In the middle of the basin four dark pipes sing one song of four notes — listen to it. Under the basin lies a pocket of sea. Saturn hangs in the north, its rings a thin bright ellipse; at noon the Sun goes behind it.

nodes.task: Fly to Uranus and aim at Miranda — a small gray moon above the planet that lies on its side. On its globe there is a dark square with a bright chevron: aim at it. Land and step out. Deadly cold: the suit needs a Heating Unit. Gravity is six hundredths.
nodes.story: A world sewn from patches: plates half a thousand blocks across, each at its own height and tilt, dark seams between them. Three coronae: the rings of Arden, the straight ridges of Elsinore and the dark square of Inverness with its bright chevron; at the point of the chevron lies a court where light must be sewn across a seam. Along the eastern edge of Inverness rises Verona Rupes — the highest cliff anyone knows. Chevronite grows in the seams and in the bright ice: twinned crystals for blocks, tiles and lamps, and the blank of a Ringwright Lens. Cliffhangers cling to the wall: leave them be. Uranus lies on its side in the sky: through the day its rings open into a target and close into a line; at noon the Sun goes behind it.

nodes.task: On Miranda, climb Verona Rupes from the east — the slope is long and gentle — walk out onto the beacon's walkway on its brink and jump west. Land in the snowdrift under the wall.
nodes.story: The wall is 270 blocks high. In a gravity of six hundredths you fall no faster than five blocks a second: the fall takes a minute, and there is time to look around — the bright chevron of Inverness lies right below. The drift of ice dust at the foot is forty blocks wide and catches anyone unharmed. Miss it, and the landing will hurt but will not kill a healthy traveler.

nodes.task: Fly to Neptune and aim at Triton — the big pale moon with a pink cap. Aim at the cap: a thread of light rises from it toward Neptune. Land and step out. The coldest place in the Solar System: the suit needs a Heating Unit. Gravity is eight hundredths.
nodes.story: A captured world: Triton runs around Neptune backwards. The cap is pink nitrogen frost in dark streaks of dust, all lying one way — downwind. Black geysers throw columns a hundred and fifty blocks high, and the wind bends them into long tails; a geyser throws whoever steps on it forty blocks up. Around the cap lies the cantaloupe crust — dimples rim to rim — and the smooth blue ice of frozen lakes behind a scarp: it is slippery. In the lake ice and in the crust lie lodes of captive ice: two Cooling Units from one set of parts, and a bucket of coolant without a pump. Plume-eaters hang in the columns. In the cap stands the Anchor Chain — nine links of dark iron, each as tall as a tower; above them the chain goes on into the sky as light. Climb it link by link. When the nitrogen wind rises, it pushes: hold on.

nodes.task: Go under the ice of Europa and wait in the dark water. First you will see a drifting constellation — lights with no body; then the whale itself comes out of the haze. Let it come within two dozen blocks.
nodes.story: In this ocean only the living gives light. The whale has never seen the Sun: it sings, and a wave of light runs down its body, a ring of light spreads through the water, and the glowing weed of the ice vault and the mats of the seabed answer it. It is curious and harmless: it passes under you and goes on. The scales it sheds — whale lumen — still hold a thread of that light.

nodes.task: The dark rock by Mars is Phobos. Dock at the Fear's Nest in its great crater, or set the ship down on the dusty top, step out and stand on the moon itself.
nodes.story: A potato of carbon-black rock twenty-seven kilometers long, grooved from end to end, with the crater Stickney a third of its width. It falls toward Mars two meters a century and will break into a ring one day. Gravity here is that of open space: a jump carries far. Mars fills a quarter of the sky.

nodes.task: The second moon of Mars is smaller and farther out. Find it past Phobos — the scanner hears a faint beacon there — land on its smooth dusty back and step out.
nodes.story: Deimos is buried in dust so deep that its craters are half-filled. Someone lives in it: the Free Haven of the Drifters, outcasts of every people, is cut into its side. They do not trade with strangers and do not shoot first — yet.

nodes.task: Fly out past Neptune to the Kuiper Belt and aim at Pluto — a tan dwarf with a pale heart on its side. Aim the crosshair right at the heart and you will enter the sky above the Sputnik glacier. Land on the ice and step out. No air to speak of, deadly cold: the suit needs a Heating Unit. Gravity is six hundredths of the Earth's.
nodes.story: The edge of the Sun's country. The heart is a glacier of nitrogen ice that slowly boils: it is cut into cells the size of a town, and in the dark troughs between them grows heart ice — blue druses of frozen starlight; break them with a pickaxe. Mountains of water ice float in the glacier like bergs, and cliffs of it ring the shore. To the west lie the red plains of Cthulhu and the blades of methane ice; a blue haze stands in layers on the horizon, and when the heart breathes out, it thickens and frost settles on the ice. Charon hangs in the north and never moves: full at midnight, dark at noon. Glacier worms swim in the troughs — do not stand on a dark edge for long. In the very middle of the heart stands a ring.

nodes.task: The gray moon beside Pluto is Charon, half its size. Aim at it from space, land and step out. No air, deadly cold: the suit needs a Heating Unit.
nodes.story: Gray water ice with ammonia in it, cratered and old; the bright crater in the north is fresh ammonia frost. The red cap at the pole is Mordor: gas that escaped from Pluto, froze here and was cooked by sunlight into tar. Pluto fills a third of the sky and never moves — the two have faced each other for four billion years. At noon the Sun passes behind it, and Pluto stands as a dark disc in a ring of blue haze. Herds of Pluto gazers — three-legged walkers with a lens for a head — stand and look at it; leave them be and they will not touch you. To the north climbs the Ferryman's Pier: stand between the pillars at its end. When dark red flakes fall, tholin crust settles on the ice.

nodes.task: Farther out than Pluto drifts a dark red rock made of two — a snowman lying on its side. The scanner hears a faint glow there. Find it beyond Pluto, set the ship down on the flat top of the larger lobe and step out.
nodes.story: Two bodies that touched four and a half billion years ago at walking pace and stuck. Nothing has happened here since: New Horizons passed it on January 1, 2019, and it is the most untouched thing anyone has visited. Nothing is built here, and nothing should be. In the bright collar of the neck and on the floor of the crater, grains of primordial matter smolder — the dust the worlds were made of. Break it with a pickaxe: the crusher grinds it into stardust.

nodes.task: Every ten to fourteen days a planet without a star stops in the Kuiper Belt for two days, each time in a new place. It gives no light. Catch its flare in the astrograph three nights running, then open the almanac in the anomaly codex: it marks the pass for your ship. In space it is only a black disc against the stars. Land before it leaves; the cold up top is deadly: the suit needs a Heating Unit.
nodes.story: A planet thrown out of its system, warmed only from within. Under a hydrogen haze lies a dark plain of ice, basalt, crystal or frost — every pass it is a new edge of the same world, and what you leave there goes away with it. Under the ice, in basins, stand warm lakes; in their ceilings, veins of relict ice, frozen while its star still shone. The cold up top is deadly: the suit needs a Heating Unit, and only the lakes are warm. Five minutes before it leaves, the ground groans; a minute before, it cracks with light. Whoever stays is thrown off: with the ship, into space; without it, home by the suit's beacon, frozen through.

nodes.task: Someone lived here. Find the hall over the warm lake — a round ruin of dark stone with a sign of a ring around a black disc — go down the stair in its middle and open what waits on the island.
nodes.story: The Orphans are a people whose star was eaten. They did not see who ate it: only a patch without stars that grew wider every night, and light running into it like water into sand. When their star became a coal, they let their world go into the dark, keeping the fire of the deep under the ice. Their caches hold records — five in all, one per pass — and relict ice. Theirs are the first words about the hunger, told by those it ate.

nodes.task: In the middle of Pluto's heart, on the flat ice, stands a ring forty blocks across. Walk up to it. From the rune stone to the south of it, look up through the opening.
nodes.story: The seventeenth gate. The other sixteen look at one another; this one looks out. It is of the same make as the gates of the worlds and five times their size, and it is broken in eight places. Each gap takes a Threshold Keystone — heart ice set in tetrataenite and osmiridium: jump up along the arc (here a jump carries twenty blocks) and set the keystone into the gap. The heart of the ring is the lowest block of its inner rim: stand in the ring and click it — it will show what it asks for.

nodes.task: Wake the Ring at the Edge. It asks for all eight links closed, six Ringwright tablets of the Sun's worlds read, and the bearing of the Wow! signal taken; the price is 128 stardust and a Hawking spark. When every line in its window is done, touch the heart with any part of the price — and step back.
nodes.story: The runes ran round the ring from the heart to the crown, columns of light stood up along its plane, and a beam went through the opening straight into Charon. Now the opening is a window: there are stars in it that are not in this sky. A thread of light stands over the ring — it is seen from the far side of the heart and from space. The ring did not wake alone.

nodes.task: Beat the keeper of the Ring at the Edge: it comes out of the opening as soon as the ring wakes, and later an offering at the heart calls it back — 4 heart ice and 32 stardust. The first sign of the fight: it rolls in a straight line — step aside at the last moment.
nodes.story: A ring that keeps a ring: it slept inside the seventeenth gate for as long as the gate stood broken. It does not hate whoever comes — it weighs them. In every phase it changes: its runes turn from blue to gold when the membrane of the Threshold is drawn across its opening, then pale to violet when rays grow from its links and the membrane becomes a window of stars. Its heart is the Threshold Key — the core of the interstellar drive (the key of a second victory crowns the Threshold Staff). When it falls, the seal on the stele by the ring falls too: the niche behind it holds the Tablet of the Threshold.

nodes.task: Defeat the Gatekeeper a second time and make the Threshold Staff around the Threshold Key.
nodes.story: The first key goes into the interstellar drive; the second can open small gates. Raise the staff: one gate stands before you, the other where you look. Step in — and step out over there; step back — and you are here again. A threshold does not ask who crosses it: a foe who follows you comes out beside you.

nodes.task: Build the interstellar drive and fit it into a module socket of a starship of class A or above (the ship console: E in the cockpit). Its heart is the rarest thing the sky road gives; Hawking sparks are caught at the flares of the disk of Planet Nine. The recipe is below.
nodes.story: The drive jumps between the stars. Stage "Threshold" reaches 1,500 light-years, "Pulsar" 8,000, "Quasar" 30,000: a higher stage is built from the one before and from what the far places give. A jump burns about six buckets of fuel — more the farther it goes — and 16 stardust; then the drive recharges for two minutes. Ships of the void and of the depths do not carry it: their far places lie in their own skies. The drive goes nowhere without a navigation record.

nodes.task: The drive jumps only to what you have recorded. Aim a star telescope at the Pleiades — the cluster behind the back of Taurus — with an imaging plate in your inventory, and left-click.
nodes.story: A navigation record is a picture of the place itself: a cluster is bright enough for any star telescope, a nebula needs the long exposure of an astrograph. Each record spends a plate. Tablets, radio logs and anomaly data can hold records too. Recorded places appear on the Interstellar map — the map key (M by default) in the cockpit of a starship.

nodes.task: In the cockpit of a starship with the drive, open the Interstellar map (M), choose the Pleiades and plot the course. Aim the nose at the course mark in the sky and hold the jump key for three seconds. Before the jump, look at the map: will there be fuel for the way back?
nodes.story: 444 light-years from home: nine named stars — seven sisters and their parents, Atlas and Pleione — and the blue dust they light. The wisps of Merope dust are blocks a ship flies through: the mining beam gathers them, and now and then the dust stays in the hold; the dense frost inside the wisps always gives it. There is no danger here. The way home is the course the drive holds by default: aim at the mark and hold the jump key. And give the scanner a pulse: the eye does not see everything behind the dust.

nodes.task: In the Pleiades, pulse the scanner: there is a dim star behind the dust. Fly to its mark, land on the pole and open what stands there.
nodes.story: The eye sees six stars in the Pleiades, and nearly every people of Earth tells of a seventh who was lost: Merope who hid her face, Electra who turned away, the sister carried off by the hunter. The seventh is real — a star too small to ignite, still warm, with a ring of ice around it. Someone found it before you and left a casket on its pole: seven stars on the lid, six of them lit. Whoever it was knew where to look.

nodes.task: Take a navigation record of the Orion Nebula — under the belt of Orion — through an astrograph, then plot the course on the Interstellar map and jump. It is three times as far as the Pleiades: count the fuel both ways.
nodes.story: 1,344 light-years from home, inside the nearest great cradle of stars. Ahead is the Trapezium: four hot stars that burnt a hollow in the cloud. Their ultraviolet wind grows toward them: the gauge under the place name fills, and a full gauge burns the hull. The shade is behind a body — a proplyd, a dark globule, an orphan planet; a heat shield module holds the wind back too. Protostars hide in dark cocoons and fire jets along their axis five seconds out of eight: do not cross them. The scanner marks the proplyds: there is something in their cores.

nodes.task: Find a proplyd with the scanner and park the ship in the shade behind its head. Step out in a spacesuit, go in through the passage on the shaded side, break the glowing shell in the middle of the hollow and take the seed from the cradle with your hand.
nodes.story: A proplyd is a disc of dust around a star not yet lit; the Trapezium blows its gas into a tail, and in the middle matter gathers into a seed. A cradle that gave up its seed goes dark and ripens again in time, so those who come after you will not find it empty. The mining beam does not take the cradle. Two seeds and the Pulsar Navigator of the radio telescope lift the drive to the "Pulsar" stage; beyond it lie the places the first stage does not reach.

nodes.task: Make a coronagraph: an attachment that hides a star behind a shutter so its faint changes show. Its recipe opens with the "Coronagraph" project at the observatory console of your station.
nodes.story: A coronagraph works from your inventory: while it is with you, the graviscope shows not the blinding star but a ring of its light around a dark shutter. Some stars in it are worth watching at night.

nodes.task: In Cygnus the graviscope shows a warm star that sometimes dims. With the coronagraph in your inventory, watch it in the middle of the night and click on it at the bottom of a dip. Three dips on three nights make a light curve.
nodes.story: The light curve is torn and uneven: what passes before the star is no planet and no cloud. It is a navigation record — the interstellar drive can jump to Tabby's Swarm now.

nodes.task: Lay a course to Tabby's Swarm on the Interstellar map and jump. A hull and a suit should be ready: the place is not empty.
In the middle of every whole panel glows an amber node. Get out of the ship, reach it and mine it with an iron pickaxe or better.
nodes.story: A surviving swarm panel folds into the light-catcher panels of a station: a second way to the light-catcher module, without pallasite lenses. Four panels and the records of the Swarm open the "Light-Catcher" project at your observatory.

nodes.task: Fly to the Archive behind the great panel and go in. Its lamps go out near Shades of Hunger — click them to light them again.
nodes.story: The Archive still breathes and keeps light in crystal plates. Its eaten wing is airless and dark. Deep inside, a niche of the Ringwrights waits for whoever comes through.

nodes.task: Build a hydrogen maser from the interferometer blueprint and set it beside the receiver of a radio telescope.
nodes.story: The maser is a clock that loses a second in a hundred million years. With such clocks the telescopes of three roads can listen as one eye: one in the Solar System, one in the Interrift, one in the Depths.

nodes.task: On the night of Sagittarius click the maser and hold the aim on the bright center for a minute. The console names the hour of the next night.
nodes.story: A night record keeps the night and the road. Records of one night from the star, void and fire roads are combined in the observatory of your own station.

nodes.task: Bring three records of one night of Sagittarius — from the star, void and fire roads — to the observatory console of your station and click it.

Reach the center of the Galaxy: jump to Sagittarius A* in a starship with Drive III (the shadow image is the record of the place) — or take the fold of the Loom in a void ship with Keel III, the well of the Crucible in a depth ship with Jacket III.
Fly a void ship with the Blind Stitch keel into the fold of the Loom in the Interrift. The fold takes its price in fuel and void shards — the instruments name it as you come close.
nodes.story: The blind stitch folded all of visible space, and a ring of lenses stood in the puncture. The dark berth took the ship: its console opens the wing for you. The way home is the veil of the fold beside the berth, and it is free.

nodes.task: Take a depth ship with the Core jacket down into the well of the Crucible in the Depths. The well takes its price in fuel and deep embers — the instruments name it as you come close.
nodes.story: The dive went through the core within the core: at the center of the world the melt turned into light. The fiery berth took the ship: its console opens the wing for you. The way home is the hot ring beside the berth, and it is free.

nodes.task: Take the fold of the Loom in a void ship with Spindle Keel III and the shadow image, open the gates of the dark berth, sew up the two leaks of the void, tear the seam of the cloth and light the dark lens.
nodes.story: A hall of seams: the leaks are false seams and the void pours out of them; the true seam was sewn on purpose, and it is torn. Hunger went fastest along the dark road: there the light has nowhere to hide.

nodes.task: Take the well of the Crucible in a depth ship with Crucible Jacket III and the shadow image, open the gates of the fiery berth, wake the three ringing anvils by striking to their beat and light the fire lens.
nodes.story: A forge at the edge of the ring: the anvils remember the rhythm of the hands that forged the rings. The fire of the depths did not go out by itself — it was given away.

nodes.task: Light all three lenses with your own hands and bring 128 each of stardust, void shards and deep embers to the heart console by the sealed door of the heart.

nodes.story: A giant cut out of the dark, with swallowed stars inside: the hunger has taken the shape of those whose warmth it drank. Blows barely touch it — but the light of a lens does, and a sewn seam, and a blow in time, and a line between two stars. Its claws and its gaze carry the cold of the void: your step drags and frost creeps over your eyes, but the Heart itself is warm — this cold cannot kill, and a Heating Unit all but shrugs it off. To call it again the core asks 8 shadow clots and 32 each of stardust, void shards and deep embers.

nodes.task: Forge the Star in the Palm in the zero-g forge of your station around the Swallowed Star: four shadow clots, two ring sparks and four gold ingots.
nodes.story: The first star it ever swallowed still burns. On right-click it leaves your palm and circles you: whatever comes near burns, and Shades of Hunger burn threefold. With practice there are three stars, and at the end they flare.

The ship the Ringwrights themselves flew, from the time before the roads were three. Every road opens to it: the sky, the rifts and the vents, the Underweave and the Underdeep — its drive, keel and jacket are one with the hull. It burns light: any fuel of any road turns to light in its lenses, and a third of each bucket is the price.

The thing that ate the light is gone, and the light it held has gone back into the roads. The frames of every gate ring flare as you come near — once on each world, for each traveler who was there at the end. The Facetkin of the Facet felt it in their veins before anyone told them.

nodes.task: Find a Prism Gate on the plains of the Facet, walk up to it and step onto the threshold between its pillars.
nodes.story: The gate that led nowhere was waiting for whole light. It opens only for the one who made the light whole; for everyone else the opening stays empty. Beyond it is not another world — only a place to stand and look. The same threshold brings you back.

nodes.task: On the platform beyond the Prism Gate, touch the Light Basin in the middle. Walk to the end of the pier: home is visible from there.
nodes.story: A cut stone hanging over the Galaxy: the whole Milky Way below and ahead, Andromeda to the right. The three roads you walked are drawn across it as three arcs, and the places you have been to shine as sparks around home. The basin gives each traveler one Whole Light to carry back, and after that it recounts the road.

nodes.task: Find a Blind Spot — with the instrument of your road or the ship's scanner — fly into it and hold the ship's light on each of its five dead hearths, then on the clot in the middle.

Take a navigation record of the Helix Nebula — in Aquarius, below the bright star Ancha — through an astrograph, with an imaging plate in your inventory. Then plot the course on the Interstellar map and jump: 650 light-years, the first stage of the drive reaches it — but the jump burns 6.3 buckets: a six-bucket tank needs a tank module.
nodes.story: Inside the Eye of God: a tunnel of gas that a dying star breathed out, teal at the pupil and red at the rim, with thousands of cometary knots on its walls, tails pointing away from the center. In the pupil burns what is left of the star — a white dwarf the size of the Earth. It burns the hull and pulls the ship in, and the tail of a knot lies in shade. The Sun will look like this in five billion years. The scanner marks the dwarf: its core is freezing into crystal.

nodes.task: Fly to the white dwarf of the Helix with a heat shield and a mining beam. Where its crust is cracked, the lattice of the core shows through: take it with the beam, quickly, before the heat gauge fills — then back off to cool down.
nodes.story: A white dwarf cools for billions of years, and its carbon and oxygen freeze into a crystal — the Gaia telescope saw stars of this kind pile up in 2019. Its crystals hold their lattice even in the time well of a black hole: they are the heart of the Chrono Cell, a station module. The other parts lie farther — beyond the first stage of the drive.

nodes.task: Rebuild the drive into the "Pulsar" stage: the "Threshold" drive, the pulsar navigator from the radio telescope, two star seeds from the Orion Nursery and a ring spark. Fit it back into the same socket.
nodes.story: By three pulsars the ship knows its place to a block — and jumps farther: 8,000 light-years, a fifth less fuel for the same jump. The Crab Nebula and Cygnus X-1 are within reach now; their records are taken by the radio telescope and the graviscope. The middle of the Galaxy and the magnetar in Vulpecula wait for the "Quasar" stage.

nodes.task: Rebuild the drive into the "Quasar" stage: the "Pulsar" drive, a quasar reference, a ring spark, four neutron dust and two disk plasma. The radio telescope assembles the reference after the third record of the quasar; the dust is in the filament wisps of the Crab, the plasma at the disk of a black hole.
nodes.story: A point that never moves, two and a half billion light-years away: with it the drive reaches 30,000 light-years, and no jump costs more than a small tank holds. The magnetar in Vulpecula is within reach — and the middle of the Galaxy, once the shadow image shows where to aim.

nodes.task: The navigation record of the Crab is not a picture but a radio log: fold the period of the Crab pulsar on the radio telescope. 6,500 light-years — the jump needs a "Pulsar" stage drive.
nodes.story: In 1054 Chinese astronomers recorded a guest star bright enough to see by day for three weeks. Its shell is a cage of red filaments full of neutron dust, lit from inside by the blue glow of electrons spiraling in a magnetic field. At the heart a neutron star spins: its two beams sweep a band around it in a steady rhythm — listen to the clicks. A beam that crosses the ship strikes the hull and throws it aside.

nodes.task: Reach the pulsar of the Crab. The beams sweep a band around it: count the rhythm, cross the band right behind a beam — on boost.
nodes.story: A neutron star twenty kilometers across, heavier than the Sun. Jocelyn Bell Burnell found the first pulsar in 1967 and jokingly named it LGM-1, "little green men": the pulses were too regular for nature. Pulsars keep time better than clocks — ships can steer by them, and the Pioneer plaque points home by fourteen pulsars.

nodes.task: Pulse the scanner in the Crab: four survey points lie in the band of the beams. Come within seventy blocks of each and pulse the scanner there — between the beams.
nodes.story: Four points around one pulsar fix its pulse from four sides — this is how navigators measure a ship's place by pulsars (SEXTANT, 2018). Each point is a clump of neutron knots: the dust of the 1054 shell gathers in the band where the beams press it.

nodes.task: Find Cygnus X-1 with the graviscope, then take a navigation record of it: aim at the black hole with an imaging plate in your inventory and left-click. 7,200 light-years — the "Pulsar" stage.
nodes.story: The first black hole astronomers accepted, twenty-one Suns heavy. It tears gas from the blue supergiant HDE 226868 — half the sky — into a white-hot disk and fires jets along its axis. Hawking bet Thorne it was not a black hole, and paid in 1990. The rim of the disk is clumps of plasma for the mining beam; closer than 300 blocks the tides crack the hull, the disk plane burns, the jets kill. And near the hole time runs slow.

nodes.task: Put a Chrono Cell on your station (its kit is below), then hold in the time well of Cygnus X-1 — 55 to 130 blocks from the hole, above or below the disk — until the station has an hour.
nodes.story: Near a black hole the clock runs slow: a minute in the well is up to an hour out there. The Chrono Cell takes that hour for your station — the refinery fills its tanks, the greenhouse its rations, the workshop its repair hours, the drones fly their routes. Eight hours a visit, no more; the tides take their share of the hull. Like Miller's planet in Interstellar — only nobody loses the years.

nodes.task: Catch three bursts of a series of the repeating source with the radio telescope dish on Vulpecula.
nodes.story: Most fast radio bursts come once and never again. One source in Vulpecula repeats: once every five days it sends three to six bursts in a night. Point the dish at it, wait for the series (the hint tells when) and straighten each arc with the dispersion wheel. Three bursts are a navigation record: the drive will find the star that shouts.

nodes.task: Jump to the magnetar in Vulpecula — thirty thousand light-years, an interstellar drive of the Quasar stage.
nodes.story: A neutron star twelve kilometers across with a field of a hundred trillion gauss. Around it hang the fragments of its torn shell; field lines glow in loops from pole to pole, beams burn out of the poles. Closer than 820 blocks the field jams the scanner, the jump and the weapons of a ship without a Magnetic Shield — and drags iron to the star. To leave, first fly out of the field.

nodes.task: Live through a starquake wave by the magnetar — ideally behind a fragment of its shell.
nodes.story: Every two minutes the crust of the star cracks. Ten seconds before, the star swells and its field lines tremble; then a white flare, and a wave runs out across the whole place at sixty blocks a second. In the open it tears the hull and throws the ship; a fragment between you and the star takes most of it.

nodes.task: Mine magnetar scale from the veins on the shell fragments — a diamond pickaxe or better.
nodes.story: The veins glitter pink and violet inside the fragments: crust tempered by the field. They lie inside the field — without a shield the scanner is blind there, so look for the glow by eye; and leave your iron armor behind: the field drags it to the star.

nodes.task: Finish the observatory project "Magnetic Shield" at your station: three radio records of the magnetar and eight scales.
nodes.story: Scale in a ring of coils turns the field aside: by the magnetar the scanner, the jump and the weapons work again. Without the shield, everything there is done blind and unarmed.

nodes.task: Build a ship of the void — the Moth or the Comb, known after the Unblinking of the Eye — fuel it with liquid pearl and rise above the sky of the End.
nodes.story: The Interrift is the void over the End where the rifts hang. Islands of end stone, flying combs and shards of facets drift in it; currents of the void carry a ship for free; caches keep the blueprints of the Prism and the Thorn. Fly into a rift to enter the sky of its world — one you have been to; home is down, to the pale disc of the End below the islands. Four peoples keep stations before their rifts.

nodes.task: Build a ship of the depths — the Salamander or the Anvil, known after the Keeper of Tears of the Lament — fuel it with coolant, fly out over a lava sea of the Nether and hold Shift: the ship dives through the lava.
nodes.story: The Depths lie under the Nether: floating rocks of basalt and obsidian, magma geodes with the fire rose, currents of magma, and below — the glowing vents of four worlds. Fly into a vent to come out in its world; rise to the vault to surface in the Nether. Caches keep the blueprints of the Lantern and the Hammer.

nodes.task: Meet any creature of the Interrift: fly up to it or catch it with a pulse of the ship scanner.
nodes.story: Four kinds live among the islands. Chorus drifters ride the currents of the void in a chain: touch a ripe one under way, and it throws the ship forty-eight blocks ahead — a chorus skip; the bush goes pale for a while and drops a pod. Skein weavers take a slow ship for a lost shuttle: they line up in a twisting chain and lead it along their thread to the nearest cache, wait for a laggard, circle above the cache and leave a bobbin; full speed scatters them. Runaway drones of the Hive settle on a slow hull as stowaways and patch it with wax as they ride, then leave a lump of it. And in the dark of the void islands waits the void eel: it springs from ambush, clamps onto the bow and drinks the tank — it lets go only at full speed in the open or in a current. Pods and glands burn in the tank of a void ship, wax patches its hull and parts into honeycomb, the thread of a bobbin unwinds into six lengths of string.

nodes.task: Meet any creature of the Depths: fly up to it or catch it with a pulse of the ship scanner.
nodes.story: Four kinds live in the heat. Magma rays weave before a ship in a braid of fire, trading sides — and scorch a hull that crowds them. Fire bubbles hang in clusters on the currents of magma: a ship or a shot that comes close makes one swell and burst, and the burst sets off its neighbors in a chain; a pearl is left where each hung. Obsidian mites sleep in obsidian: disturb it with a pickaxe or the mining beam, and the brood swarms the hull, pries at the hold for a few seconds and carries the cargo off one piece at a time to its druse — move and they fall off, shoot one on its way home and it drops what it took. And the scanner lies: a cache mark on a lone rock may be the lantern of a cache angler, which strikes the bow from ambush and hides again — look closely: its mark breathes slower than a true one, unevenly, and a red ember glows in its middle. Scutes make heat tiles and patch a depth ship, pearls grind into blaze powder, scales turn obsidian to crying obsidian, a lantern makes two navigation crystals.

nodes.task: Go back to the magmascope in the Nether. Now that you have been to the Depths, it hears more than four vents: strike the magma and listen for what answers wrongly — an echo with no vent, a double beat, a ring that goes out.
nodes.story: Four anomalies of the depths are found the way vents are — listen and hit the rhythm — but each has its own catch. The Fifth Echo is hollow and is fixed by three strikes from different places. The Heartbeat sends waves across the whole magma. The Wandering Heat will not stay under the crosshair. The Cold Spot drinks the ring of a strike. Each record gives a seismogram, one per anomaly a day; three seismograms on different days, and the anomaly is tracked. Cards and the real stories behind them are in the Anomaly Codex.

nodes.task: Among the rocks of the Depths hangs a dark shell two hundred blocks across, with glowing seams and one bright mouth. The ship scanner marks it. Fly into the mouth and step out on the floor.
nodes.story: Inside is a forest of fire rose crystals, some taller than a house; the shell keeps most of the heat of the Depths outside. The crystals sing: strike one and it rings to an even beat — and its first note is a wave that hits and throws. In the heart of the largest crystals a great fire rose glows.

nodes.task: Take a great fire rose whole. A ringing crystal shatters its heart; a crystal falls silent for the one who strikes it three times in time with its own ringing.
nodes.story: The move is the one the magmascope taught: listen and hit the rhythm. A large crystal rings slowly and low, a small one fast and high. A strike out of time, or a pickaxe in a crystal that has not been calmed, and the wave comes at full strength. A calmed crystal is silent for two minutes: enough to cut down to the heart. A great fire rose splits into four ordinary ones.

nodes.task: Find the Fifth Echo in the magmascope: it marks a hollow place deep in the Depths, far to the south and below the layer of rocks. Fly a depth ship there and dive into the glowing crack of the shell.
nodes.story: A hollow world with a small sun in the middle: the land curves up and hangs overhead, rivers and all. It is the one place on the three roads where you can breathe without a suit. Firemoss grows toward the sun; among the hills lie the ribs of giants, and at the start of the world there is a great hearth. The sun flares every few minutes: the sky whitens, a line counts the seconds — get under a firemoss crown or a rock: the open ground burns. Where flares have scorched the moss away, suncoal lies bare: one piece burns in a furnace as long as a bucket of lava.

nodes.task: Find the Cold Spot in the magmascope — the place where a strike goes dull. In the Depths a geode hangs there with no glow in its seams. Go in; take a Heating Unit with you, not a Cooling Unit.
nodes.story: Rime in the middle of the fire road. The crystals are dead and broken and no longer sing; it is as cold inside as the Depths are hot outside. In the broken crystals sit growths of shadow, and light dims next to them. A growth breaks into shadow clots: in the cabin of a depth ship one clot is three buckets of coolant.

nodes.task: Track the Wandering Heat in the magmascope. Once every eight to twelve days an island-bubble rises in the Depths where the heat has stopped — the ship scanner will mark it. Land on it before it sinks.
nodes.story: The island stands for a day. A lens of smoldering crust comes up out of a pillar of flame; on it are bubbles with fire rose bushes inside and nests of deep embers. What you mine is yours; the rest goes down with the island — it warns a minute ahead.

nodes.task: Find the Heartbeat in the magmascope: a slow double beat below all the vents. In the Depths a platform with a broken golden ring hangs over that place. Land on it and read the plaque.
nodes.story: Through the mouth in the middle of the platform the sealed well can be seen far below; something beats under its crust. The well will wake for the one who has tracked the Heartbeat. The road beyond the threshold is not laid yet.

nodes.task: The anvil at the mouth of the well on the threshold is waiting. Look at it: it will show what it still lacks — the Heartbeat tracked, the Tablet of the Hearth read, and the forge paid in deep embers, suncoal and fire roses.
nodes.story: Three blows of the anvil, and the well answered: a column of melt struck up through the mouth, and the seals of the crust crumbled. A spiral stair goes down the throat of the well into the Crucible — a vessel hung in the void under the plate.

nodes.task: Go down the well into the Crucible. It is hot inside: a heat suit or a Cooling Unit, and something to drink. Four tiers: the casting yard, the halls of hammers, the bellows and the quench. Each gate wants its own work done.
nodes.story: Gold runs down the chutes by itself, and the gates decide where. The anvils of the halls each ring to their own beat. A blank from the quenching hearth keeps its heat for thirty breaths. The molds here are cut for rings nine paces across; the guild of the gilded smiths left its notes on the lecterns — they came to learn the casting.

nodes.task: At the bottom of the Crucible is the Giant's Hearth. Lay suncoal on its altar: the one who still works there will come out. Jump his waves, crouch under his high rings, stay off the pools; when the hearth goes cold, keep to the embers.
nodes.story: He was not angry. He watched whether you could hold the heat — and when he saw it, he gave it away and lay down. His heart is the Last Ember: one victory, one ember. The altar will call him again for another offering. The way up is the Crucible Flue in the treasury: its draft carries you to the Threshold.

nodes.task: Wrap the Last Ember in ember obsidian and adamant, over a heat shield: a jacket for a depth ship.
nodes.story: With the jacket the hull holds the heat of the Crucible Well. The well leads down to a fiery dock — but the dock is silent for now: it opens to a crucible jacket III with the shadow image. The first stage already dives deeper than the Depths, where the magmascope strikes.

nodes.task: Forge a hammer around a second Last Ember: two adamant ingots, the ember, a netherite ingot and a grip.
nodes.story: The ember keeps the Giant's rhythm. On right-click the hammer strikes the ground three times, and from every blow a ridge of heat runs ahead along the ground: foes on their feet are thrown up and burn, foes in the air are spared. With practice the last blow rolls an unfinished ring after them.

nodes.task: The heddle before the darned doorway of the Threshold is waiting. Look at it: it will show what it still lacks — the Knot traced, the tablets of the First's Nest and of the Enderhome read, and the warp paid in void shards, condensed void and the First's shell.
nodes.story: The heddle lifted the warp four times, and the darn came apart from top to bottom. Behind the frame the mouth of a shaft opened: a stair goes down under the deck into the body of the loom hung in the dark of the Knot.

nodes.task: Go down the shaft into the Loom. Four warps hang one under another — the Facet, the Hive, the Breath, the Eye. A seam is torn and a tear is sewn by hand and eye together; knots are tied in the order of their figure. Take the Lens: some signs show only through it.
nodes.story: In each warp there is a hall where the thread of its world is woven, and that thread goes through the cloth from the vault to the floor. The Shades of Hunger eat the light in the dark halls; the moths fly to any lamp. The lowest gate wants the spool of the warp: it is walled up in the spool room.

nodes.task: At the bottom of the Loom, in her nest, the Spinner keeps the warp. Lay condensed void on the altar of the nest. Cut her tethers with a blow, kill what crawls out of her cocoon, sew the rifts she spins — then she loses the thread.
nodes.story: The Spinner let go of the warp. Her heart is the Spindle: a ball of the warp that still glows. A spindle keel for a void ship is made around it, and, from the second victory, a weapon: the Warp Thread. The way up is the Backstitch in the treasury: its thread draws you to the Threshold.

nodes.task: Build the Spindle into the keel of a void ship: firstshell, condensed void, void thread and a hull armor module around it.
nodes.story: The warp threads of the Loom run into a fold of the dark half a thousand blocks behind its frame. A hull with a spindle keel goes through it — but the dark dock beyond the fold is silent for now: it opens to a spindle keel III with the shadow image. The first stage already stitches to the underside of the sky.

nodes.task: The second Spindle goes into a weapon. Defeat the Spinner once more and craft the Warp Thread: the Spindle at the point, condensed void beside it, a shaft of the First's shell on a grip.
nodes.story: The thread ties foes together and drags them into one knot, and when it snaps, it strikes each of them.

nodes.task: The Tablet of the Warp teaches you to look from the underside. In a riftscope in the End turn the sky inside out with the right mouse button and find the sign of a place on the cloth: a slow spiral of loose threads. Trace it from the edge to the eye.
nodes.story: The pattern of the Warp Sargasso is pinned to the "Pattern" map of a void ship. Where its sign hangs on the underside, there its course lies in the Interrift.

nodes.task: Lay the course on the "Pattern" map of a void ship of class A or above with a spindle keel. Leave the island field into open void, turn the nose to the course and, holding the jump key, lead it along the pattern stitch by stitch. It costs liquid pearl, void shards and thread spools.
nodes.story: The cloth gave way: the Underweave, the underside of the space between worlds. Your thread runs behind the ship — rewind along it home for half the pearl, and the spools come back.

nodes.task: The Tablet of Rings teaches you to strike down to the core. In a magmascope in the Nether hold a strike for a second and a half: the bowl falls through, the shells of the world show as rings, and the places of the fire road answer from their depth. Find the double echo and strike twice in its rhythm.
nodes.story: The section of the Ringwoodite Sea is marked on the "Section" map of a depth ship: 520 km down, in the transition zone of the mantle. Seismologists know the Earth's interior the same way — only by its waves.

nodes.task: Lay the course on the "Section" map of a depth ship of class A or above with a crucible jacket. Go below the island field of the Depths, turn the nose down and strike the jump key in the pulse of the place. It costs coolant, deep embers and iron blocks for ballast.
nodes.story: Under the feet of the world lies an ocean in stone: blue ringwoodite holds water in its crystal. To go home, drop the ballast and rise on the plume for half the coolant; the ballast stays below.

nodes.task: In the Ringwoodite Sea the cliffs sweat water. Cut the wet ringwoodite on their faces with the ship's mining beam: the coolant goes straight into the tank of a depth ship, the stone into the hold.
nodes.story: Ringwoodite holds water in its crystal lattice. In 2014 a diamond from Juína in Brazil was found to carry hydrous ringwoodite inside: there may be as much water in the transition zone as in all the oceans.

nodes.task: The mephisto worms bore toward the wettest veins. Follow a worm to the mouth of its burrow in a cliff and go along the burrow to the vein: it gives more water and hides inclusion diamonds.
nodes.story: A burrow is lined with wet stone: the worm drinks the rock as it goes.

nodes.task: Find the mephisto worms of the Ringwoodite Sea at the mouths of their burrows. They lead a slow ship to a burrow; one of them sheds its cuticle in thanks.
nodes.story: Named after Halicephalobus mephisto — a nematode found in 2011 in a gold mine in South Africa, 1.3 km underground, where nothing was supposed to live.

nodes.task: Look in the faces of the cliffs of the Ringwoodite Sea — and more often in the wet veins — for diamonds with a drop of water sealed inside.
nodes.story: A diamond is a pressure vessel made by the planet itself: what it closed in the deep, it carries up unchanged.

nodes.task: Make a pressure capsule: an inclusion diamond for the window, wet ringwoodite and the cuticle of a mephisto worm for the seal. Its nine cells keep the pressure of the Underdeep.
nodes.story: Put a stack into the capsule as into a bundle: click the stack with the capsule. What lies inside does not feel the surface.

nodes.task: In the magmascope find the section of the Bridgmanite Halls — three even strikes and a long pause, deep at 265° — and dive there: 1,600 km down, into the lower mantle.
nodes.story: A chain of halls overgrown with amber beams the size of towers — the Cave of Crystals of Naica, a hundred times larger. This is not a geode: the crystals do not sing, they hold each other up.

nodes.task: Cut a bridgmanite beam at its seam — the glowing band in the middle — so that it comes out whole. Lines of light show which beam holds which: cut first those on which nothing rests, or the strained one bursts in a chain.
nodes.story: Bridgmanite is the most common mineral in the Earth — about 38% of its volume — and yet it was only named in 2014, after a grain in the Tenham meteorite.

nodes.task: Carry bridgmanite up whole: put it into the pressure capsule before you surface. Without pressure it crumbles to dust.
nodes.story: Nobody has ever held this mineral in their hands. You hold it.

nodes.task: Rebuild the crucible jacket: the Lining, a Deep Sounder from the station observatory, two hydrous ringwoodites and a ring spark. Hydrous ringwoodite comes from the water intake of the Ringwoodite Sea.
nodes.story: The Caisson holds down to 5,000 km: deeper places answer on the "Section" — the Buried World and the Iron Ocean. Dives to nearer places cost less coolant.

nodes.task: Build the Core jacket from the Caisson, a shadow image and a ring spark. The fourth part is a core of the Buried World; without it the jacket takes a giant's marrow, adamant, hydrous ringwoodite, an inclusion diamond and a deep ember — dearer, but with no far dive.
nodes.story: The Core jacket holds to the very center — the Core Quarry at 5,800 km — and passes the well of the Crucible: the fiery berth waits below.

nodes.task: Take its section with the magmascope: a deep strike, and its echo comes late — a pale mark shows when it should have come; strike the real echo, not the expected one. Then dive there with a "Caisson" jacket: 2,800 km down, seven iron blocks of ballast.
nodes.story: On the floor of the mantle lies a continent of foreign rock that never mixed with it. Under Africa and the Pacific seismic waves slow down in two regions the size of continents; in 2023 it was proposed that they are the remains of Theia, the planet whose impact gave birth to the Moon. Plumes rise from their edges.

nodes.task: Take a core sample: break a core seam with the ship's mining beam — a beacon of lights stands over each. There are three: the seabed, the city, the ash. Once the core is out, the layer above slides — you have two seconds to back off.
nodes.story: A core is a column of layers: the deeper, the older. This one reads from the bottom up: a sea, then a city, then ash. There is nothing above the ash.

nodes.task: Reach the middle of the Buried World. The instruments show the way: the closer, the colder.
nodes.story: Where this world had a core there is a smooth empty bowl. This is the bottom of the mantle, one of the hottest places there is — and it is cold here. The warmth was not lost. It was taken.

nodes.task: Carry a core up whole: put it into the pressure capsule before you surface. Without pressure its layers come apart. The "Core" jacket needs a whole one.
nodes.story: The layers of the core were pressed together by 130 gigapascals. Only pressure still holds them as one.

nodes.task: Take its section with the magmascope: on the shell of the outer core there is a shadow — an arc where no echo comes. The echo answers at its two edges in turn: strike the left edge, then the right one. Then dive with a "Caisson" jacket: 3,500 km down, nine iron blocks of ballast.
nodes.story: Shear waves do not pass through liquid. In 1906 Oldham saw their shadow on the far side of the Earth, and in 1914 Gutenberg measured its edge: the Earth has a liquid core. Its iron flows — and that flow makes the field every compass obeys.

nodes.task: Over the sea of iron, iron snow sticks to the hull: the ship grows heavy and sinks toward the sea. Shake it off with a boost — the snow goes into the hold. Nine make a block of iron.
nodes.story: Iron snow is a hypothesis: crystals of iron that form in a cooling liquid core and settle through it — in Mercury, in Ganymede, and at the edge of the Earth's own solid core.

nodes.task: Circle a column of melt three times on the move, 30–120 blocks from its axis: the field will charge a coil. The column pulls the ship in and spins it — keep your distance.
nodes.story: A conductor moving through a magnetic field carries a current — Faraday, 1831. In a spinning core the flow of iron gathers into columns along the axis; the lines of the field you see in the haze are wound by them.

nodes.task: Take its section with the magmascope: deep in the shadow of the outer core, almost at the center, there is a faint answer — three even beats. Strike it three times in a row. Then dive with a "Core" jacket: 5,800 km down, fifteen iron blocks of ballast.
nodes.story: In 1936 Inge Lehmann found faint waves where there should have been none — in the shadow of the liquid core. Something inside it reflected them: a solid core within the liquid one. Her paper was titled "P′".

nodes.task: The ball is one crystal of iron, and its axis runs north to south. Turn the nose of the ship along the axis and cut the crystal with the beam: three times as much. A pickaxe, too, goes three times faster along the axis.
nodes.story: Waves cross the solid core faster along the axis of the poles than across it: its iron crystals lie one way. In 2023 a core inside the core was found — there the crystals lie another way.

nodes.task: The sinew of the First Thread remembers both sides of the cloth. Take three sinews, sargasso yarn and messenger nacre to the zero-g forge of your station.
nodes.story: Every arrow of the String Bow has a twin: a mirror opens at the target, and the second arrow flies out of it to meet the first. Each hits weaker than a plain arrow, and the twin carries no enchantments — but there are two of them.

nodes.task: The swatches of the Sampler's loom keep the stitch the Ringwrights walked by. Take swatches, messenger nacre and scar thread to the zero-g forge of your station.
nodes.story: The needle carries you eight blocks ahead through walls. For three seconds after the stitch your hand hurts no one — and what is sealed, the needle does not take: neither unbreakable walls nor the masonry of a dungeon whose master lives.

nodes.task: Scar thread pulls together what was torn — that is how the Scarfield was mended. Build a module of scar thread and sargasso yarn for a void ship.
nodes.story: The rig mends the hull by itself, a point every four seconds — once ten seconds have passed without a hit. It will not save you in a fight, but the ship comes home whole.

nodes.task: A string that sounds on both sides can show a ship on both. The blueprint is traded for knots of the Underweave — or known to one who struck the chord of the First Thread. Build the module of string sinew for a void ship.
nodes.story: For eight seconds a twin of the ship flies alongside: drifters, their torpedoes and the creatures of space strike at it. Once a minute — and the masters of space are not fooled.

nodes.task: The organ pipes of the plumes in the Buried World are basalt that still remembers the melt. Cut plume basalt with the beam of your ship and take it, with deep embers and salamander crystal, to the zero-g forge of your station.
nodes.story: A strike of the rod raises columns of melt in a line ten blocks long: they toss foes up and set them on fire. Water puts the melt out — in the rain the rod only hisses.

nodes.task: Core iron is one crystal with an axis. Take core iron, iron snow and a charged coil of the Iron Ocean to the zero-g forge of your station.
nodes.story: Blows from the front run along the axis of the shard and land a third weaker. Blows in the back find its cleavage — turn to face the foe.

nodes.task: Hydrous ringwoodite carries water through the mantle. Build a still on your station and feed its retort with the stone.
nodes.story: The still turns the stone into coolant for the tanks — take it with a bucket — and into air: whoever is aboard has their suit tank topped up.

nodes.task: The field of a world is made by iron that flows. The blueprint is traded for hallmarks of the Underdeep — or known to one who charged a coil in the Iron Ocean. Build the works of iron snow and a charged coil on your station.
nodes.story: In 1919 Joseph Larmor proposed that the field of the Sun is a dynamo that feeds itself; the Earth's turned out to be one too. The station's is small, but it burns nothing: all the station's work runs a third faster.

nodes.task: Here it is the sky that turns, not the ground: it speeds up, stops and goes back. While it moves, shear drags the ship sideways and tears the hull inside the shaft. Wait for the window of the sky to stand over the shaft — half a minute of stillness — and go down to the very bottom.
nodes.story: The solid core turns on its own: it floats in liquid iron. Around 2009 its turning against the mantle slowed, stopped and went the other way — it seems to swing like this about once every seventy years.

nodes.task: Skeins of amber yarn hide in the tangles of the Sargasso. Cut a tangle with the ship's mining beam — the scanner marks the tangles with skeins.
nodes.story: Sargasso yarn is warm to the touch. It goes into the "Lockstitch" keel.

nodes.task: Cross the rings of tangles to the quiet eye of the Sargasso — between the tangles, without touching them — and record the spawning with the ship's scanner.
nodes.story: Eels spiral above the nest, and thousands of glass larvae turn around it like a galaxy. On Earth eels swim to the Sargasso Sea to spawn — and no one has ever seen it.

nodes.task: Catch a glass larva in the eye of the Sargasso: an empty glass bottle in your inventory and the mining beam — or a bottle in hand, outside the ship.
nodes.story: A transparent leaf glowing from within. The larvae of real eels are just as transparent; Johannes Schmidt found the smallest of them in the Sargasso Sea in the 1920s.

nodes.task: Find the sign of the Scarfield on the underside of the sky — a breathing seam of rough stitches — and stitch there.
nodes.story: A field of rifts sewn shut. They are roads to worlds closed for good: a scar breathes, opens for a few seconds, and the wind of another world blows through.

nodes.task: Some scars have come loose. Aim at the knot at the end of a weak scar and lead the stitch along the seam to the other knot before its fistula opens.
nodes.story: A darned scar is quiet. In scar thread the fibers lie side by side, not in a basket weave: a scar holds no more than four fifths of the strength of skin.

nodes.task: Look into an opening fistula from close by: what lies beyond it is recorded. Four different worlds blow through the fistulas.
nodes.story: A sunny sea, amber dunes, an ice plain, an emerald sea under rain — worlds behind the scars. Their roads are sewn shut.

nodes.task: One of the scars is not like the others. Listen to the fistulas.
nodes.story: Behind one scar there is nothing: no wind, no light. More rifts were sewn shut than there are worlds behind them.

nodes.task: Rebuild the spindle keel: the Basting keel, a Nacre Navigator from the station observatory, two sargasso yarns and a ring spark. The yarn is spun from the tangles of the Warp Sargasso.
nodes.story: The Lockstitch reaches 600 threads: farther pieces can be pinned to the "Pattern" — the Sheer and the Sampler. Stitches to nearer places cost less pearl.

nodes.task: Build the Blind Stitch from the Lockstitch keel, a shadow image and a ring spark. The fourth part is a pattern card from the loom of the Sampler; without it the keel takes a warp spool, a void lens, sargasso yarn and condensed void — dearer, but with no far stitch.
nodes.story: The Blind Stitch reaches 1,500 threads — as far as the First Thread — and passes the fold of the Loom: the dark berth waits behind it.

nodes.task: Find the sign of the Sheer on the underside of the sky — a rose window whose rim trembles like gauze in the wind — and stitch there. It is reached by a Spindle Keel II.
nodes.story: Here the cloth is worn down to gauze, and through it, from the other side, shine the worlds you have walked — mirrored, like stained glass seen from behind. Do not hurry near the gauze: faster than forty blocks a second it tears.

nodes.task: Hover over a window in the gauze where a world shines and send a scanner pulse.
nodes.story: A world from the underside: everything the other way round. Some think the Cold Spot of the cosmic microwave background (WMAP, 2004) is the trace of a touch from a neighboring universe — a supervoid big enough to explain it was never found (2017).

nodes.task: Take the underside of every world that shines for you in the Sheer.
nodes.story: The whole road walked, seen from the other side of the cloth.

nodes.task: Find the sign of the Sampler — a twill staircase sliding along the diagonal — and stitch there. It is reached by a Spindle Keel II.
nodes.story: The Ringwrights' workshop: an embroidery hoop four hundred blocks across with a trial cloth of space. Every square has its own weave and its own rule; in the middle stands a jacquard loom.

nodes.task: With the mining beam, cut out the tags in the middle of the squares — plain weave, twill, satin and basket weave.
nodes.story: Four weaves, four rules of space: plain is as usual, twill pulls along the diagonal, satin is a mirror with snagging loops, basket weave is slow, but blows do not get through.

nodes.task: At the loom in the middle of the hoop, punch the card with the beam to the pattern on the wall above it: a hole lifts a thread. Three cards, and the loom weaves.
nodes.story: The loom wove a band of space, and new stars lit up in it. Jacquard's loom (1804) wove by punched cards; Babbage took them for his Analytical Engine, and Ada Lovelace compared its patterns of numbers to the flowers and leaves of the loom.

nodes.task: Find the sign of the First Thread — a straight line whose antinodes swing — and stitch there. Only a Spindle Keel III reaches it.
nodes.story: One red-hot thread through the whole place: the first thread of the warp of the dark road. Do not come close — it cuts the hull and the thread home. Behind it everything is seen twice.

nodes.task: Touch the thread with the beam at the nodes between the anchors — ½, ⅓, ¼ — and hold for a second on each. Away from a node the thread plays false.
nodes.story: Three true tones: the thread sang, the doubles merged into one, and for a second the cloth was transparent — far off, in shadow, a dim ring. Where the thread leads has no name.

nodes.task: Finish an order from a contract board: the board stands by the dock of every station of a people. Take an order, do the work, hand it in at the same board (a parcel, at the board of the station it is addressed to).
nodes.story: Every station offers one order of each kind a day. Ore: bring ore of the belts or the islands. A parcel: take the crate to another station of the same space before time runs out — the board loads it into the hold of your ship on the pad. A survey: fly to the point and pulse the ship scanner. A rescue: a shuttle in distress waits at the point — fly up to it with hull plates and a fuel canister. The goals of taken orders are marked in the sky of space and on the star map; no more than three orders at once. Stations pay with the supply of their road — stardust, void shards, deep embers — and with the trust of their people.

nodes.task: Become an Acquaintance of any people that keeps a station: hand in orders at its board and finish the errands of its keeper.
nodes.story: Each people counts its trust on its own. An Acquaintance gets survey orders, a dock a fifth cheaper and cheaper stalls; a Friend gets rescue orders, still cheaper stalls — and only a Friend is trusted with the last errand of the keeper, the one that gives the key to the vault. A parcel delivered late costs trust with the sender.

nodes.task: Take the Ring Race at a contract board, lift off and fly through the first ring of light over the station: the clock starts there. Twelve rings in a minute and a half; then hand the race in at the board.
nodes.story: The course runs in a circle around the station, above the rocks and the islands, and changes every day. The next ring burns brightest and a beam points from it to the one after. A ring missed costs five seconds, not the race; time up — fly through the first ring again. The best time of the station and the name of its pilot stay on the board: beat it for extra trust. A scout takes the circle with time to spare, a hauler only just.

nodes.task: Take a Bounty at a contract board and bring the trophies it names — teeth of rockgnawers or tallies of drifters.
nodes.story: Rockgnawers come in swarms to a ship that works slowly in an asteroid field; a cannon brings them down, full speed shakes them off. Every fifth bounty handed in pays with a ship module as well.

nodes.task: Become Kin to any people: keep handing in the orders of its board and the tasks of its settlements.
nodes.story: Kin is the people you chose. One of them will join the crew of your station, their dock and stalls are a third cheaper, and a shipyard or a dock raises a ship to class S only for someone who is Kin to a people of that space. Striking one of them costs trust at once — the line above the hotbar says how much and why.

nodes.task: Become Sworn to a people — the last step of trust.
nodes.story: The Sworn receive the great gift of the people — a thing that cannot be bought — a title and their colors on the ship. Nothing on the way to the end of the roads needs it: it is for those who found their people.

nodes.task: Fly a void ship to a station of a people of the rifts. Each hangs seven hundred blocks from the rift of its world, on the side of the End, in a harbor cleared of islands; a scanner pulse marks it. Among the islands the autopilot stops before the first one — fly the last stretch by hand.
nodes.story: Four peoples keep a station by their rift: the Seam Prism of the Facetkin is a crystal with a deck like a splinter; the Drifting Comb of the Comb Keepers is seven cells, and ships land on the cap of one; into the Vigil Eye of the Lashkin a ship flies through the pupil; the Long Breath of the Glassbreathers is a blowpipe with a glass bubble, and the pad is its mouthpiece. Docks sell liquid pearl. A jump to a station you have visited ends inside its harbor, nose to the dock: from there the autopilot brings the ship to the pad. The errands of station folk and the keys to their vaults are the same as in the Solar System.

nodes.task: Find the broken world in the Interrift and set foot on it. It hangs in the empty quarter between the rifts of the Eye and the Facet, seven and a half thousand blocks south of the End; closer in, a ship scanner pulse marks it. Land on the crown — the flat top with the lights.
nodes.story: The shell of a world that came apart at the seams: dark crust outside, a smoldering mantle beneath, shards of the core still burning in the middle. The cracks glow; in the breaks lie veins of shard glass — it goes into lamps and frames. The pieces are reached by leaping: gravity here is weak, the void between them is not.

nodes.task: Read all six steles in the ruins of the Shards: one by the landing pad on the crown, four on the terraces of the upper pieces, the last in the bowl of the lowest piece, right under the core.
nodes.story: Each stele is the hand of someone who saw this world end. A stele stays where it stands: every reader keeps their own count. The first reading of each brings two void shards.

nodes.task: Outline the Knot in a riftscope: beyond the Facet rift the sparks fly around an empty place — lead the crosshair around its rim with the button held. Then fly a void ship into that dark blot of the Interrift and take three seam casts: ship scanner pulses from three different sides of it.
nodes.story: The Knot is a blot two thousand blocks wide where the light of a ship dies: the deeper, the darker. It is the same dark stuff as the cloud in the Main Belt — something was hidden with it. Near the very middle the dark parts.

nodes.task: Reach the middle of the Knot and land at the frame of the loom. A scanner pulse inside the Knot marks its middle.
nodes.story: A loom frame half a hundred blocks tall: the warp threads glow, the doorway in the warp is darned shut. The Loom behind it sleeps: waking it will take three seam casts, two tablets and a payment. The heddle in front of the doorway shows what is still missing.

nodes.task: Take three bearings on the Call of the First in a riftscope: high in the sky of the End, between the Hive and the Breath, rings spread from one point — lead the crosshair along the three notches. The Nest becomes a jump target. Land on the northern rim and set foot on the bowl.
nodes.story: A bowl of end stone ringed with egg-cliffs of obsidian; in the middle lie the spine, the ribs and the skull of the first dragon. In the hollows stands its breath, a lilac haze: it burns everything alive except the folk of the End. One egg is broken — around it lies firstshell, which neither dragon nor wither can break. In the jaws of the skull is a niche of the Ringwrights.

nodes.task: Get scales from the void wyrmlings that hatch from the small clutch in the middle of the Nest, and rivet them onto firstshell at a crafting table.
nodes.story: Wyrmlings hunt over the bowl in twos and threes; the lilac haze does not burn them, and a struck one blinks behind your back. Shell under scale is plating the void does not gnaw: a shipyard asks for eight sheets of it to raise a ship of the dark road to class S.

nodes.task: Find the slab with the chorus forest in the west of the Interrift, seven and a half thousand blocks from the End — closer in, a ship scanner pulse marks it — and set foot on it. Do not look the hosts in the eye.
nodes.story: Endermen carried blocks for those who set the rings — and still carry them. Here stand three ring frames nobody finished, with stacks of blocks at their feet, and a long hall with doors three blocks tall: built for their height, not ours. In the hall lie piles of messenger nacre and a niche of the Ringwrights.

nodes.task: Sit out a void tide in the Interrift behind stone: when the warning comes, stand so that an island or a wall is between you and the wave — it comes from the west. A riftscope shows the tide a day ahead: a murky wave low in the sky of the End.
nodes.story: Once every twelve days a wave of void rolls across the whole Interrift in a minute. In the open it strips a quarter of the hull of a ship; stone holds it. After the wave, crystals of void are left on the islands nearby.

nodes.task: Fly a depth ship to a station of a people of the vents. Each hangs seven hundred blocks from the vent of its world, on the side of the Nether vault, in a harbor cleared of rocks; a scanner pulse marks it. Among the rocks the autopilot stops before the first one — fly the last stretch by hand.
nodes.story: Four peoples keep a station by their vent: the Hanging Anvil of the Gilded hangs on chains, and ships land on its face; the Wandering Cap of the Fruiting Folk is a mushroom with a hall under the cap; the Last Tear of the Mourners is a drop of dark glass with its mouth in the belly; the Giant's Palm of the Giantkin is an open hand of bone with blue fires on the fingertips — the palm is the pad. Docks sell coolant. A jump to a station you have visited ends inside its harbor, nose to the dock. The last errand of each station gives the key to its vault.

nodes.task: Craft the Emitter Heart and build the dish around it: 7 × 7 emitter plates with the heart in the middle and a pylon three blocks high on each corner plate. The missing blocks show as ghosts.
nodes.story: A phased array of forty-eight lenses and four focusing pylons: the dish gathers everything this world can give into one beam. Open the heart and bring it what it asks for — a Station Seed, stardust, meteoritic alloy of the belts and the matter of this world (every world asks for its own). The sky above the heart must be open. Then hold the launch button: ten seconds of charge — and the beam goes to the zenith. It is seen for thousands of blocks, day and night. One emitter per world for each player; an orbit holds eight stations for everyone.

nodes.task: Launch the orbital emitter: the beam carries the Station Seed to orbit, and the core of your station condenses there out of light.
nodes.story: The station hangs in the orbit of the world it was raised from; its shell cannot be broken; inside there is air and the gravity of home. Step onto the heart of the emitter — the beam lifts you to the station; the lift pad in the hall takes you back down. The core has four sockets: use module kits on them. The Dock is a bay behind a force curtain — fuel, repairs, and the place where your called ships arrive. The Hangar folds ships from the dock pad into six berths and brings them back. The Cabin has a bunk: lie down once, and you will wake there. An outpost holds three modules; the scanner marks your station, and it is a jump target from anywhere on the road.

nodes.task: Open the console of the Observatory on your station and finish a research project.
nodes.story: Data are the anomalies you have recorded in the codex; substances are samples brought from them. A project takes real minutes and goes on while you are away. When it is done, the observatory opens a recipe: a ship module that uses what you learned — a direction finder, a gravity anchor, a radiation screen, a solar sail, a cloak, a throat stabilizer, a wave rider; the Interrift and the Depths have their own. The window shows what is missing and where to find it.

nodes.task: Use a Station Tier kit on any sealed socket of your station: a second drum is built under the core.
nodes.story: Each tier adds four sockets and room for more modules: an outpost holds three, a station six, a citadel ten, a ring fourteen. A service shaft with a ladder opens between the decks. Every module has a console and a trade of its own. The Refinery turns comet ice, crystals, regolith and coal into road fuel in the station tanks — the dock then fuels your ship for free. The Workshop stores repair hours — the dock mends the hull with them — and raises the tier of a ship module for stardust. The Greenhouse ripens rations for its owner and feeds everyone aboard. The telescope of the Observatory needs neither night nor clear weather, and its console sweeps the system for anomalies and the comet. The Storehouse is the hold of the station.
