The Orbital Yard and the Workshop need a station of the second level; the emitter window shows the level, the sockets taken, and what to build next.

nodes.task: Earn "Kin" trust with a people, build Crew Quarters on your station and show a Crew Contract to anyone of that people: one of them will move to the station.
nodes.story: A station grows by the plan of its builders: a Station needs 16 osmiridium plates, 8 pallasite lenses and one people that knows you; a Citadel needs 32 plates, 4 comet cores and two peoples that call you friend; a Ring needs 16 light-catcher panels, 8 comet cores and three peoples that call you kin. The Station Tier kit takes them from your inventory and the hold. A Station houses two of the crew, a Citadel six, a Ring ten — one from each people. Each brings a gift: the spore keeper doubles the greenhouse, the ice catcher speeds the refinery, the cargo master guards the drones, the bell ringer warns everyone aboard. The duty board in the quarters lists who lives here and what they give.

nodes.task: Build a Drone Bay, give a Cargo Drone to its route board and collect the pay when the drone is back.
nodes.story: A drone flies between your station and the station of a people that knows you: it takes the road fuel of the refinery and the rations of the greenhouse and in twenty minutes brings emeralds and the supply of that space. One flight in ten is caught by drifters and loses half its cargo. A Station keeps one route, a Citadel two, a Ring three. The Light-Catcher module speeds up all the work of the station — twice as much at Mercury and Venus.

nodes.task: Make a spacesuit module for zero gravity — an MMU pack, mag boots or a safety tether — and fit it into the torso at a suit rack.
nodes.story: Out of the ship, open space has almost no weight: a jump carries you away, a blow spins you off into the dark. The MMU pack walks you there: your gaze leads, jump and sneak go up and down, and when you let go it holds you in place — while the charge lasts. Mag boots hold you on metal: the plating of a station, the iron of an asteroid, the hull of a flying ship and the back of the Visitor. The tether hooks to the ship you stepped out of and reels you back beyond thirty-two blocks. The torso has four sockets: air, charge and warmth take theirs, so choose.

nodes.task: Build the Zero-G Forge module on your station (it needs a station of the second level) and forge something in its chamber.
nodes.story: In the glass sphere between the magnet columns metal hangs in emptiness: nothing settles by weight, and drops of different metals merge as they never do on a planet — in 1973 Skylab grew alloys this way. Open the forge console: the book on the left lists what it can forge; a click lays the substances out from your inventory, and the button starts the chamber. The work goes on without you; the piece waits in the output cell. A goldsmith of the Gilded in your crew makes every recipe a fifth cheaper.

nodes.task: Forge a piece of the star gear of the Solar road: Meteoric Plate, the Widmanstätten Blade, the Comet Bow, the Pulsar Rod, the "Wow!" Compass, a Mounted Star Seed or the Visitor's Sail.
nodes.story: Each has its own place, and none is the best: the plate is for open space, but storms love it; the blade pulls those in iron and knocks arrows aside; the bow leaves a freezing tail; the rod strikes twice as hard on the beat and half as hard off it; the compass only points — and costs stardust; the seed heals in the light and hungers in the dark; the sail glides, until a blow folds it. Hold the gear key over any of them for the details.

nodes.task: Forge an item of the Crab Nebula or Cygnus X-1: the Horizon Spear, the Neutron Maul, the Neutron Ring or the Cygnus Chronopendant.
nodes.story: Neutron dust of the Crab weighs like mountains, and the disk plasma of Cygnus remembers how time thickens at the horizon. The spear opens a well where everything moves three times slower — you too, if you step in; the maul squeezes a crowd into a heap and stuns it, but drags at your step; the ring makes a blow from a fall land like a star and the landing hurt more; the pendant slows time around you when you are hit hard — and then time catches up.

nodes.task: Forge a piece of the Warp Shroud (from the Interrift) or the Crucible Plate (from the Depths).
nodes.story: The dark road and the fire road each dress their own. The Warp Shroud hides you — foes notice you from closer — and the whole shroud catches you if you fall through the bottom of the world, once every five minutes; but in bright light it is thinner. The Crucible Plate is for fire up close: burning foes take more damage, the first seconds in lava do not burn, but it is heavy, and cold and water crack it.

nodes.task: Read the Tablet of Hunger in the Swarm Archive — it holds the blueprint — and forge the Lightbearer in the zero-g forge.
nodes.story: The Ringwrights kept light from the things that eat it not with walls, but with more light. In your hand the Lightbearer cuts Shades of Hunger twice as deep; near it a Shade burns, lamps do not go out and the dark does not fall on you. Raise it, and dawn floods the hall: Shades burn and flee, the rest are dazzled, the lamps light again. Against anything else it is a weak blade.

nodes.task: Get food from another world. Each world has its own plants and beasts: a fruit is planted in the soil of its world or on a hydroponic bed, where it grows five times faster — on Earth, only on the bed. Raw meat drops from creatures and is cooked in a furnace, a smoker or on a campfire; a dish is made at a crafting table from the food of the same world.
nodes.story: The food of a world helps you live in it: Warmth and Coolness hold off its cold and heat, Acid Ward its acid, Air Reserve lets you breathe a little without a tank. On the Moon it is the earthshine bulb, the hopper haunch and the Sea of Tranquility stew; the Lunarian herders sell both food and seeds. The plants of the worlds need no air: they grow without a dome.

nodes.task: Mine an ore of another world. Each world has two or three, set in its own rock: on the Moon ilmenite, which smelts into titanium, and selenite. A crusher turns raw ore into two dusts — twice the metal.

nodes.story: There is no strongest gear: each piece has its role — a crowd, a tough foe, long range, speed, protection from its own world. The ring chakram of Saturn is thrown and comes back to the hand, cutting every foe in its path; the wraith-iron scythe of the Ash sweeps blue fire in a half-circle and gives you back health from each foe; the black diamond greatsword of Neptune finishes off the wounded. A weapon has an ability — on right-click or on a hit; it recharges only after it has worked. Hold G over an item in any window with slots to see its details: the model, every number, the levels of mastery and where to find it. Weapons and artifacts also lie in dungeon chests; armor can only be crafted; the hearts of masters become weapons of their own.

nodes.task: Slay enough foes with a weapon of another world for it to grow to the second level. Every foe slain with it in your main hand gives it experience — the tougher the foe, the more; peaceful animals give nothing.
nodes.story: Mastery lives in the weapon itself and passes from hand to hand with it. Every weapon has five levels, and each strengthens the ability: the crater hammer raises more crystals, strikes harder, cuts the legs and at last fans the rift out into three lines. The level is in the tooltip; the experience and what every level gives are on the details screen (hold G), and when a level is reached, a line above the hotbar says what it gave.

nodes.task: Make a piece of armor of another world: the crater carapace of the Moon is forged from crater tortoise plates, titanium and selenite on an armor lining.
nodes.story: Armor is worn over the spacesuit, in the ordinary slots, and it is only made — no chest holds it. Each set has a strength and a real drawback, both in the tooltip; its gifts grow at two and at four pieces worn. The carapace takes blows but every piece slows your step; two pieces let you hide in the shell by crouching, all four turn a fall into a blow to the foes around. The lead armor of Venus keeps out its acid but sinks you like a stone in water and lava; the glider pelt of Saturn makes you light and quick but guards you poorly.

nodes.task: Make an artifact of another world: the selenite pendant of the Moon is the core of a selenite stalker in a gold setting.
nodes.story: Artifacts are worn in the slots of a slot mod (Trinkets; on NeoForge also Curios) — a ring, a necklace, a belt — and work while worn. Without one the mod runs as usual, but an artifact cannot be put on, and its tooltip says so. The selenite pendant flashes when you are hit: whoever struck you is blinded and slowed. The quicksilver ring of Mercury quickens your step and carries you up one-block ledges without a jump, but lowers your armor; the sigh pearl of the Breath lets you push off the air once in every jump; the float belt of Jupiter swells in a fall and lets you drift down.

nodes.task: Set the Selenite Heart in a titanium crown: two selenite focuses, the heart, a riveted crater plate and a grip make the Colossus Scepter. The heart goes into it whole, so it is one scepter per victory.
nodes.story: The heart of the Colossus has not forgotten how to raise stone: on right-click selenite guards rise around you and strike your foes with shards while they stand. It does not hit hard itself — its strength is in those who stand beside you; with mastery the guards grow in number, stand longer and shatter as they leave.

nodes.task: Forge the Twilight Core into a blade: golden sulfide for noon, hollow salt for midnight, the core between them, a quicksilver capsule and a grip.
nodes.story: The seam of the Terminator runs down the whole blade. On right-click a wave runs out split along your gaze: to the right it is noon and sets foes ablaze, to the left it is midnight and freezes them in place. At the highest mastery a second wave follows with day and night swapped.

nodes.task: Make a whip of the Acid Matriarch: her Caustic Heart between two acid glands, a sealed lead plate and a grip.
nodes.story: The tongue is still alive in its way. On right-click it catches the foe in your sights, poisons it and drags it to you; a master or anything too heavy does not budge, so the tongue drags you to it instead — across a gap, up to a ledge, into the fight.

nodes.task: Set the Storm Heart in a cage at the guard: three plates of phosphor bronze for the blade, a storm coil for the cage, the heart and a grip make the Leviathan's Wing. The heart goes into it whole, so it is one blade per victory.
nodes.story: The whale's hunger is in the blade. Every hit on a foe gathers a storm over it; the fifth hit on the same foe brings the lightning down — it strikes and stuns, and the whale drinks it, healing you. A hit on another foe starts the storm anew. With mastery the whale drinks deeper, the bolt grows heavier, the storm gathers faster, and at last it strikes twice.

nodes.task: Set the Hexagon Core in a pernach: two blocks of blue ice for the flanges, a serrated rim for the crowns, the core and a grip.
nodes.story: On right-click the ring on the head breaks into crowns that circle you: they cut every foe who comes close, throw it back and chill it, and shatter arrows and spit that fly past them. The pernach is for being surrounded. With mastery there are four rings, then six, sharper and colder, and at last, leaving, they break free and cut whatever is in their way.

nodes.task: Hang the Cryo Heart on a chain: two diamond druses for the hail, the heart, an iron chain and a grip make the Gatherer's Flail.
nodes.story: The heart has not lost the Gatherer's habit. On right-click the flail throws its hail into a ring around you; the stones roll back to you wherever you go, strike and freeze the foes in their way, and the ones that reach you settle on you as an ice shield. In a crowd the hail strikes; alone, it shields. With mastery there is more hail, it rolls through foes, the shield thickens, and at last the gathered cold bursts out.

nodes.task: Make a blade of the Locked Wind: the Gale Heart, two black diamond edges, a black diamond and a grip.
nodes.story: The wind still wants out. On right-click a wall of wind runs along your gaze: it strikes every foe it catches and carries it before it to the end — the crowd is swept away, and off the edge. Whoever stands behind a block is in the wind's shadow; masters only take the blow. With mastery the squall grows wider, colder and stronger, runs farther, and at last a second squall follows the first.

nodes.task: Set the Queen's Jelly in the hub of a fan: four chitin scales for the ribs, an amber cell, the jelly and a grip.
nodes.story: The scent of the Mother is still in the jelly. On right-click it spreads around you, and the foes it reaches take you for their Mother: for a while they leave you alone and fight each other and anyone the call missed. Masters and guardians do not obey, but the charmed fight them too, and every foe they slay counts toward the fan's mastery. With mastery the call reaches farther, the swarm fights harder and longer, more foes hear it, and at last the fallen pass the call on.

nodes.task: Set the Hematite Heart between two banded plates: with a grip and a scorpion stinger for a pommel they make the Tyrant's Claw. The heart goes into it whole, so it is one claw per victory.
nodes.story: The claw has not forgotten how the Tyrant leapt. On right-click you leap where you look, onto the feet of the foe in your sights, and where you land a crown of hematite spikes bursts out and throws back everyone around. The fall does not hurt; with mastery the core grows red-hot and sets foes alight, and at last you can leap twice.

nodes.task: Set the Heart of Living Gold in an anvil head: two salamander fuses, the heart, a gilded slag plate and a grip.
nodes.story: The coal in the heart still beats to the rhythm of the anvil. On right-click circles light up under the foes where you look, and a moment later an anvil falls into each — whoever steps out in time is spared. With mastery the anvils grow more numerous and heavier, and at last they splash burning living gold.

nodes.task: Bind the Giant's Marrow into a spine: two bone lamellae, the marrow, soul marrow and a grip.
nodes.story: The blue fire of the marrow never warmed anyone; it only takes. On right-click cold streams reach for the foes around you and for a few seconds drink their warmth: they take frost and damage, and you heal for every stream. Run too far or hide behind stone, and the stream breaks — for them and for you.

nodes.task: Grow a staff from the Mother Spore: two felted cap plates, the spore, a hypha cord and a grip.
nodes.story: Everything that lives in the Mycelium is her spores. On right-click a spore flies into the foe in your sights and sprouts; a moment later it blooms, poisons everyone around, and a spore sprouts in each of them in turn. The thicker the crowd, the further the garden spreads; a foe killed before it blooms bursts at once.

nodes.task: Cage the Heart of Sorrow on a rod: two dense plates, the heart, a sorrow core and a grip.
nodes.story: Wherever the Keeper walked, the air grew heavy. On right-click a circle lights up under the foe in your sights and tears pour into it: nobody inside can jump, fliers are dragged down to the ground, and at the end grief crushes them all — those caught in the air harder.

nodes.task: Grow a blade around the Lens of the Unblinking: a gaze lens for the edge, the heart, tanned grazer hide and a grip.
nodes.story: He did not blink for nine days; his lens blinks for you. On right-click you stand where you were looking — through foes and over gaps, but not through walls — and where you stood an eye opens: the foes around it go blind, slow down and lose you. At the highest mastery the eye bursts behind you.

nodes.task: Set the Archon's Prism in a staff: two faceted plates, the prism, a refraction prism and a grip.
nodes.story: The archon kept the light in order; now its prism keeps one ray in order — yours. On right-click a white ray strikes where you look and follows your gaze until it meets a foe or a wall. Every burn in a row on the same foe is hotter: hold the ray on one strong foe and it melts; let it slip and the heat starts over.

nodes.task: Set the Wyrm's Lung in a horn: two storm rods, the lung, cloud felt and a grip.
nodes.story: On the crown of the spire the wyrm fenced off its prey with pillars and lightning; now the fence stands around you. On right-click a ring of fulgurite pillars rises, and lightning crackles between them: whoever touches it is shocked and thrown back, and those caught inside are thrown out as it rises. You may walk out of it; foes come in only through the lightning.

nodes.task: Build a coal generator: it burns anything a furnace burns and makes energy. Machines share energy by beams of light: with a grid tuning fork, click one machine, then the other, and a beam joins their lenses.
nodes.story: A generator turns heat into motion and motion into current. Every machine here comes in four versions: the next is assembled from the previous one and a machine core, works faster and takes more upgrade cards.

nodes.task: Join two machines with a beam: click one with the grid tuning fork, then the other. A beam needs a clear line: a block in the way breaks the beam until it is removed, but glass lets it through. Mk1 lenses reach 24 blocks, Mk4 lenses 48; for more, put a grid pole or a resonator between them, and lead the beam into a sealed room through a lens bushing. A sneak-click with the fork puts beams out.
nodes.story: Energy runs along a beam as pulses of light, in the direction of flow: the more current, the faster and brighter they run, and an idle beam is dim. The crystal of a resonator sets its reach — quartz 24, moonstone 32, fire opal 40, methane ice 48: click the resonator with a new crystal. Cheaper and shorter: a beam mirror turns a beam round a corner, a beam prism splits it in three.

nodes.task: Build an induction emitter and give it a beam: it powers every machine that uses energy in its field, without beams. Set the radius in its panel — up to 4 blocks for Mk1, up to 10 for Mk4.
nodes.story: Nothing is free: a quarter of the energy only warms the air. An economizer card saves some of it, a field amplifier widens the field. Short arcs show which machines the emitter feeds.

nodes.task: Make a pair of entangled resonators, put them where you like — at the Earth base and at the Moon base, say — and join each to its grid with a beam. Then click one with the tuning fork, then the other: the pair is entangled.
nodes.story: The pair shares one store of energy: what one end takes from its grid, the other gives to its own, at any distance and between worlds. A double spiral of light rises from each end into the sky: sparks climb it where energy leaves and fall where it arrives.

nodes.task: Build a battery block and join it to the generator with a beam: it keeps what the machines do not use. A cube of eight blocks grows into a large battery, of twenty-seven into a huge one.
nodes.story: Charged batteries also fly: each rocket flight drains one. A charging station fills portable batteries in sunlight; a charging gantry fills the rocket straight from the grid, by a beam.

nodes.task: Build an electric furnace: it smelts twice as fast as a stone one and needs no coal, only a beam from the grid.
nodes.story: Heat from current has no smoke and no ash; on a world without air there is nothing to burn anyway.

nodes.task: Build a crusher. Raw ore goes in, two dusts come out, and each dust smelts into an ingot: twice the metal. Other worlds' rock goes in too: impact glass becomes optical glass, scorched crust becomes briquettes. Spare parts go in as well: a hull plate, a valve or a compressor gives back some of its metal, never more than half.
nodes.story: Every world is a quarry once you know what its stones are made of. The crusher knows the raw ores of other mods too — by the common c: tags they become two dusts of that mod — and the machines of other mods grind our ores.

nodes.task: Build a spectral laboratory and give it a beam. Then three steps. 1. Click it with a sample: an ore, a metal, a mineral, ice, a bone — the item's tooltip says "Sample for the spectral laboratory". 2. When the rainbow lights up on its screen, click it again: the spectrum opens. 3. Drag the ruler until the teeth stand on the lines, click the lines nothing explains, and press "Identify".
nodes.story: The arc burns the sample, the prism spreads its light, and lines stand on the screen: every substance has its own. This is how Kirchhoff and Bunsen learned in 1859 what the Sun is made of without leaving Heidelberg.

nodes.task: Record your first standard. 1. Click the laboratory with a simple sample: ice, a bone, an ingot of iron or lead (the tooltip of such an item says "Sample for the spectral laboratory"). 2. When the rainbow lights up on its screen, click again: the spectrum opens. 3. Click every line and press "Record a new standard". After that, mixtures: pick standards below and drag the ruler until every tooth stands on a line.
nodes.story: The scale of every sample is off by its own amount, so the ruler has to be found by the pattern of the lines. What no standard explains is something new — unless there are two new things at once: then find a simpler sample. Some recipes open only to those who know what a thing is made of.

nodes.task: Make a spectrograph. By day, click a telescope with it to catch the light of the Sun; at night, while observing, right-click a planet you have found.
nodes.story: Light carries the lines of everything it passed through. The air of a world is written in its spectrum: you can know what you will breathe there before you fly.

nodes.task: Find the line that belongs to nothing on Earth: study the light of the Sun. You will need the standards of hydrogen, sodium, calcium and iron.
nodes.story: A yellow line a hair from the sodium pair. Janssen and Lockyer saw it in 1868 and named the element after the Sun; on Earth helium was found only twenty-seven years later.

nodes.task: Find a world whose light has oxygen next to methane: take the spectrum of a planet with the spectrograph through a telescope. You know this world better than any other — but you cannot see it from its own ground.
nodes.story: Oxygen and methane destroy each other: where both remain, something keeps making them. This is the sign astronomers look for in the light of distant worlds.

nodes.task: Build an ore scanner. A click sends a pulse: it shows nearby ores that hold the substance of a standard you have recorded. Sneak-click picks the standard. The charge is redstone dust from your inventory.
nodes.story: The scanner does not look for "ore in general" — it looks for lines it knows: what your handbook lacks, it cannot see. It finds lead in galena too, and sulfur in cinnabar.

nodes.task: Find an unknown mineral, a strange alloy or alien dust — in a ruin chest, in a shipwreck, on the master of a world — and identify it in the laboratory. An identified sample opens: there is an item inside.
nodes.story: The mineral hides a gem, the alloy can be repeated, and the dust is older than the Sun. Which is which, only the lines will tell.

nodes.task: Identify a part of a creature in the laboratory: a gland, a core, a plate, marrow. Whoever knows what a creature is made of hits it harder.
nodes.story: Gypsum splits along its layers, old bone is porous, glass is full of stress. The gain is small, but in a long fight with the master of a world it shows.

nodes.task: Record every standard of the handbook of spectra: the ores of all worlds, the light of the Sun and of the anomalies, the unknown samples. The laboratory pays stardust for each new standard, and richly for the whole book.
nodes.story: A table with no empty cells left: everything your worlds are made of is called by its name.

nodes.task: Build a melt pump and set it at the shore of the golden sea of the Forge or of a lake of tears in the Lament. It draws the melt out of the sources beside it: gold cools to slag and gives gold ingots, tears set into weeping glass and give sorrow quartz.
nodes.story: The sea does not end. Your patience and your charge will. The pump takes three more melts: the living gold of the spires gives more gold, the pupil glass of the Eye sets into gaze crystal and gives lens crystals, and plain lava cools to obsidian and gives magma cream — the binder of the cryo still.

nodes.task: Build a solar panel and put it under open sky. It works by day; the farther from the Sun, the weaker.
nodes.story: Light falls off with the square of the distance: at Jupiter a panel gives a twenty-seventh of what it gives on Earth. A reflector card adds a third.

nodes.task: Build a bioreactor and feed it kelp: kelp and light make oxygen. It needs energy; oxygen leaves through pipes.
nodes.story: Algae make most of the oxygen on Earth. A catalyst card squeezes a quarter more out of the same kelp.

nodes.task: Build an oxygen tank and join it to the bioreactor with oxygen pipes. It stores oxygen and fills spacesuits.
nodes.story: One unit of oxygen is one breath. A tank of the first version holds fifty thousand: enough for a long stay without air.

nodes.task: Build an air blower and put it in a sealed room: it fills the room with air. Doors must be airlock doors.
nodes.story: The blower finds the room itself: air spreads from the block until it meets walls. One hole, and it leaks out.

nodes.task: Build an oxygen dome: it holds a ball of air with no walls at all. The field needs moonstone — it is mined on the Moon.
nodes.story: A field leaks: the dome spends far more oxygen than a sealed room of the same size. A membrane card closes a fifth of the leak.

nodes.task: Make all four parts of the spacesuit and put them on at a dressing table. It protects only as a full set. A new torso is empty: open an oxygen tank while wearing the suit, and it fills it.
nodes.story: The torso holds five minutes of air on its own; bottles add more. Modules go into its four sockets on a suit rack. An oxygen tank and a suit rack fill the suit right on you: open them while wearing it. The torso also refills itself wherever there is air: under a dome, in a sealed room, by a rocket with life support.

nodes.task: Build a dressing table: the spacesuit is put on and taken off only there. Open it and put the four parts into the sockets.
nodes.story: The suit goes on under armor and takes none of its slots, so any armor can be worn on top of it. Without the table the suit cannot be put on at all.

nodes.task: Make a hydroponic bed and plant seeds on top of it, as on farmland: wheat, carrots, potatoes, beetroot, melons or pumpkins. It needs no water, no soil and no air, and lights the sprout itself.
nodes.story: Roots stand in a nutrient solution instead of soil, so the bed works on the Moon as well as at home, and the crop grows about twice as fast. Off Earth it is the only way to farm: ordinary farmland grows nothing there, even under a dome. In Earth's villages the hydroponist works at such a bed and sells bread, apples, golden carrots and the beds themselves.

nodes.task: Build a suit rack, give it a beam and a pipe, and open it while wearing the suit: the modules of your torso appear in the sockets, and the rack fills it with oxygen and charge. A spare torso can be put on the rack instead.
nodes.story: A cooling unit keeps out the heat of a lunar day, a heating unit the cold of its night; both spend charge. A solar film charges the suit in the sun, an antigravity unit keeps gravity down to Earth's on heavy worlds.

nodes.task: Build a fuel depot and join it to the fuel plant with fuel pipes: the plant sends fuel down the pipe when it has no empty canisters.
nodes.story: A canister is a thousand units of fuel. The depot drains full canisters and fills empty ones, but holds one kind at a time: rocket fuel, helium-3, liquid pearl or coolant.

nodes.task: Build a launch gantry, put it by the launch pad and pipe fuel to it: it finds the rocket itself and fills it through a hose.
nodes.story: The gantry takes the fuel the rocket needs: a lunar rocket runs on rocket fuel, a heavy one on helium-3.

nodes.task: Build a charging gantry, put it by the launch pad and give it a beam: it charges the rocket with a beam of its own, a battery at a time.
nodes.story: Eight thousand units of energy make one rocket battery. With a gantry, no battery ever has to be carried.

nodes.task: Build an acid scrubber for Venus: inside its field the sulfuric clouds do not corrode. Without it, only a spacesuit with an acid-proof coating survives outside.
nodes.story: The clouds of Venus are droplets of sulfuric acid; the surface below is hot enough to melt lead. The scrubber drives the air through alkali and keeps a ball of clean air around itself.

nodes.task: Build a pearl liquefier, give it a beam and feed it ender pearls: it melts them into liquid pearl, the fuel of the rift shuttle. Put in empty canisters and it fills them — or pipe it to a launch gantry by the dock.
nodes.story: Two pearls make a portion of liquid pearl; the shuttle holds ten. The liquid keeps the pearls' habit of slipping through space, and that is what carries the shuttle through a rift.

nodes.task: Build a cryo still, give it a beam and feed it ice and magma cream: it distills coolant, the fuel of the diving bell. Put in empty canisters and it fills them — or pipe it to a launch gantry by the winch.
nodes.story: Blue ice gives the most, a plain block of ice the least; one magma cream binds a portion so it does not boil away in the Nether. The bell spends the coolant to stay cool in the lava.

nodes.task: Build two pneumatic stations and join them with pneumatic tubes. Put one right against a chest and switch it to "Sending", the other against another chest — it receives. Capsules will carry the items through the tubes. Samples in the filter sockets decide what a station sends or takes.
nodes.story: A capsule flies only when there is room at the other end. Tubes branch freely: the item goes to the receiver with the highest priority, a filtered one before an unfiltered one, then the nearest. A red lamp and steam mean the receiver has nowhere to put things. Stations work with the chests and machines of other mods too.

nodes.task: Build a storage terminal and storage cells and stand the cells right against the terminal and each other. Give the terminal a beam and open it: everything in the cells is in one window, with search and sorting.
nodes.story: Click takes a stack, right-click half, Shift puts it in your inventory; Shift-click in your inventory stores a stack. A pneumatic station "On request" against the storage sends orders through the tubes: Ctrl+click an item (Cmd on a Mac). A broken cell keeps its contents.

nodes.task: Build an auto-assembler and a recipe card. Take the card in one hand and a sample of a part in the other and use the card: it remembers the crafting recipe. Put the card into the assembler and the parts into its tray.
nodes.story: A pneumatic station "On request" beside the assembler brings missing parts from a storage with another such station. A hopper below takes the finished parts. Several recipes for one item: use the card again.

nodes.task: Build an energy converter and put it right against a cable or a machine of another mod: it joins our beam grid with their energy, both ways.
nodes.story: The machines of this mod take and give the energy of other mods by themselves — RF, FE, EU: on Fabric through Team Reborn Energy, on NeoForge through its own energy. The converter is for where an explicit bridge is wanted: one block, and the beam grid sees a foreign machine.

nodes.task: Fill a bucket with a liquid. An empty bucket is filled by clicking a machine that gives the liquid — a fuel plant, a fuel depot, a pearl liquefier, a cryo still; the molten gold of the Forge and the tears of the Lament are scooped right from the sea and the lakes. A bucket is the same as a canister, a thousand units: click a craft or a piped machine with it to pour it in.
nodes.story: Spilled liquids live their own life. Molten gold burns like lava and sets into slag in water; tears hold you like water but bring sorrow — slowness and weakness; rocket fuel burns, and lava sets it alight; helium-3 boils away in seconds; liquid pearl throws whoever touches it aside, like a chorus fruit; coolant freezes and ices the water nearby. A dispenser pours buckets by itself, and the tanks and pipes of other mods know our liquids.

nodes.task: Make an airlock door and set it into the wall of a sealed room: two blocks wide and three tall, it slides apart at a click and closes by itself three seconds later. While closed, it holds the air.
nodes.story: Every full block holds air, and so do glass panes and pipes; an ordinary door does not, and a room behind it is never sealed. Two airlock doors with a lobby between them make a real airlock: open them one at a time, and the room keeps its air.

nodes.task: Raise a machine to the next version or make an upgrade card. The next version is made of the previous one, a machine core and two hull plates. The Mk2 core takes moonstone from the Moon; the Mk3 core, the metal frost of Venus and the fire opal of Mars; the Mk4 core, the golden sulfide of Mercury and methane ice from the bergs of Uranus. A core is tuned with the dust of a road: Mk2 with stardust, Mk3 with deep embers, Mk4 with void shards.
nodes.story: Every version is twice as strong and roomy as the one before — Mk4 is eight times the first — and has one more socket for cards in its panel. Nothing is free: the Accelerator works half as fast again but eats two thirds more energy; the Economizer saves a sixth; the Field Amplifier widens a dome or a field by a quarter; the Expander adds half again to the capacity; the Catalyst squeezes a quarter more out of fuel and kelp; the Membrane closes a fifth of the leak; the Reflector gives a solar panel a third more light; the Conductor lets half as much again through a battery or a tank. A card fits only where it has work to do.

nodes.task: Build a gravity generator: inside its field gravity is what you set, from a quarter of Earth's to twice it. Its heart is a gravity pylon and a Machine Core Mk2 — the core takes moonstone.
nodes.story: On the Moon a jump carries you three blocks up; on Jupiter you cannot climb a step. The field makes a home out of both. The wider and stronger it is, the more energy it eats.

nodes.task: Make a multimeter out of a copper coil and click a machine with it: it shows what the beam grid gives, asks for and stores. A manometer out of a valve does the same for oxygen and fuel pipes.
nodes.story: Spare parts are not dead weight: a hull plate in one hand patches worn gear in the other, a copper sheet patches a little, and the crusher gives back part of the metal of any part.

nodes.task: Build a lift drive and guide rails. Put the drive at the bottom of a shaft three blocks wide, facing the shaft — the cabin runs in front of its face — and stack the rails on it: the cabin climbs as high as the stack. Put a call post on every floor within five blocks of the middle of the shaft, give the drive a beam and click a post.
nodes.story: In the cabin a jump takes you a floor up and a sneak a floor down; a click on its floor opens the list. Calls from several floors wait their turn. If the power fails between floors, the cabin holds on its brakes: sneak to let it creep down to the floor below. A higher mark is faster and climbs higher.

nodes.task: Build two jump beacons and put one at each of your bases in the same world. Give both a beam, stand on one, click it and choose the other in the list — then stay on the beacon until the jump has charged.
nodes.story: A jump costs charge by distance, and only you go, with what you carry. Sneak-click opens the panel: there the owner lets guests in. Between worlds beacons do not jump: that is what gates, rockets and ships are for.

nodes.task: Build a drone nest and a route card. Sneak-click a chest with the card for "from", then another chest or a machine for "to". Put the card into the nest and give the nest a beam.
nodes.story: A sample in the other hand, when you use the card, tells the drone what to carry. The drone flies straight or arches over an obstacle, takes only what the other end has room for, and charges in the nest. It is slow: where a tube reaches, pneumatic mail is better.

nodes.task: Make a suit module and fit it into the torso on a suit rack. The Moon is hot by day and freezing by night: a cooling unit and a heating unit hold that off while the suit has charge.
nodes.story: Four sockets, nine modules: oxygen bottles for ten and twenty minutes, an air recycler that saves a third of the oxygen, a cooling unit, a heating unit, a power cell of 8000 ⚡, a solar film that charges in daylight, an antigravity unit for heavy worlds and an acid-proof coating for Venus and the Breath, which needs no charge. Venus wants the cooling unit and the coating, the giants the heating unit, Jupiter the antigravity.

nodes.task: Make a knapsack. Open it with its key (F9), or use it from your hand. With a slot mod (Trinkets; on NeoForge also Curios) it is worn in the back socket; without one the knapsack works right from your inventory.
nodes.story: Cards go into its sockets: "Pickup" sends what you pick up to the same items in it, "Feed" refills your hand as you build, a small suit tank or a power cell keeps a reserve for the suit. A higher mark has more cells and sockets and keeps what was inside.

nodes.task: Live through an event of a world: be in that world when it ends — anywhere in it. Every few days something happens in each world, and a banner says what: on Earth a solar or lunar eclipse, a parade of planets, a supernova; on the Moon a meteor shower or a moonquake; on Jupiter fragments of a comet dive into the clouds one after another; in the Forge the sea of gold crusts over, and you can walk far out across it.
nodes.story: In a solar eclipse the day turns to night and the undead walk without burning; in a lunar one the dead come at midnight. In a parade of planets worlds found through a telescope on Earth bring double stardust and every gate lets you through for free; a supernova can be caught in the telescope sight for stardust and a nova shard, and while it burns, hints are free. Each world has three events of its own, and their danger always shows first — a ring of fire, a rune, cracks, a toll; the reward lies close to the danger. The gate of a world waits for one particular event of its own: the meteor shower on the Moon, the great dust storm on Mars, the lightning season in the Breath.

nodes.task: See the weather of a world in full force. It comes and goes by itself, without a banner, and lasts minutes: on Earth northern lights sway over the north at night and morning fog fills the lowlands before sunrise; on the Moon dust hangs glowing at dawn and micrometeorites strike; on Mars dust storms rise and dust devils wander.
nodes.story: Weather is humbler than events, but it changes the world a little. Hail and micrometeorites wound a bare head — a helmet takes the blow; wind pushes you about under the open sky — crouch or get under a roof. Some weather helps: the Exhale of the Mycelium lets you breathe without a tank for a few minutes, the Clouded Lens of the Eye hides you from monsters, light pillars of the Facet show where to dig; stardust settles with micrometeorites, and gold nuggets with the gold haze of the Forge.

nodes.task: Make astral tiles: eight blocks of polished deepslate around stardust. A stonecutter turns the tiles into slabs, stairs, panels, columns, cornices, moldings, beams and the Compass Rose and Orbits mosaics; the astral lamp, lantern and sconce take moonstone.
nodes.story: The Observatory set — blued metal, brass and turquoise light — is for a telescope to stand among: the Starry Sky Panel and the constellation panels cut from it, observatory glass in a brass frame. Trophies come back from flights: the statue of a world — the Moon Statue is an astral lamp over three astral tiles with a moonstone and two selenite shards — and its stained glass, eight glass blocks around a treasure of that world: a selenite shard for the Moon, a fire opal for Mars. Every world has a building set of its own — a planter for any plant, a relief, a druse, a mural that fits itself together from neighboring blocks: the Moon Phases Mosaic, the Giant's Rib of the Ash, the Eye Lantern that blinks now and then; and the rock of every world is cut into polished blocks, bricks, slabs, stairs and walls. All of it lies on the decor tab of the creative inventory.

nodes.task: Trade with a villager of a new craft. Earth's villages now have houses of a new kind — an observatory, a rocket workshop, a fuel depot, a power house, a greenhouse — and a jobless villager takes the craft of the workplace beside him: an astronomer at a telescope, a rocket engineer at a drafting table, a fuel technician at a fuel plant, a power engineer at a charging station, a hydroponist at a hydroponic bed.
nodes.story: The specialists of the villages save long chains of crafting, but not the journey: the astronomer sells optical glass, lens blanks and polished lenses, later stardust and a primary mirror; the rocket engineer sells hull plates, heat tiles, nozzles, turbopumps and avionics; the fuel technician sells canisters of fuel and, at the higher levels, of helium-3; the power engineer sells charged batteries, and as a master a charging station; the hydroponist sells food and a hydroponic bed. They pay emeralds for glass, amethyst, copper, coal and even lunar regolith.

nodes.task: Whoever set the gate rings left writing beside them. Find a gate ring and click the stele of dark stone with carved signs on its dais. On Earth the ring stands on a dais of deepslate, often far away: a village astronomer sells a chart to it.
nodes.story: Each sign is a whole word. Touch an inscription and the stone shows you a fresco: what is in it is what the words are about. Pick a sign, then a picture you have met — when every sign of the phrase is right, the phrase comes together. The lexicon tab of the journal keeps everything you have learned.

nodes.task: Read a whole phrase. A sign that looks like the gate ring is probably "ring"; a sign inside such a ring is the name of a world; a sign standing on a foot is something done. A wrong guess costs nothing — the phrase just does not come together.
nodes.story: Understood signs glow on the stones for you — and only for you: another player sees their own reading. The same sign glows in every inscription where it stands, so each new phrase is easier than the last.

nodes.task: Next to many inscriptions stands a stone casket with a ring for a lock. It stays silent until its words are read — the same as on the stele. Read the inscription beside it, then open the casket.
nodes.story: A casket gives every reader a gift of their own, once: in multiplayer nobody takes yours. Words that seal doors work the same way: read the inscription by a word-sealed passage, and the seals flare up and crumble.

nodes.task: In the court of the Lunarians stands a stele of the Slab-Setters with the Lunarian reading cut beneath it. The meaning is given; which sign is which word is not. Read it.
nodes.story: That is how the hieroglyphs were read on Earth: a stone with the same words in a known language. Every people remembers scraps of the script — ask the elders about the signs.

nodes.task: Read the inscriptions by the gates of four worlds. The world name in each one stands in a ring: the planets are signed with the same signs Earth's astronomers use.
nodes.story: Each gate inscription tells what its world keeps: a warden, a fire, a sky. Someone taught Earth these signs long ago — the ring of Earth is older than any road.

nodes.task: Understand sixteen signs of the Ringwright script — a full ring, as they would say.
nodes.story: The Ringwrights counted by sixteens: a whole ring is sixteen. You read their stones now the way the peoples cannot: whole phrases, not scraps. What is left of the script waits in ruins, dungeons and on the tablets beyond the worlds.

nodes.task: Something on the Moon answers ships. The Lunarians speak of a slab that rings when somebody hangs in the sky above it. Find it and hold your ship over it for a while — low, right above the stone.
nodes.story: The slab — one by four by nine, without a single seam — kept silent while people came to it on foot. It was waiting for one who comes by the sky. When a ship hung over it, the slab rang, a pattern ran across the regolith, and a niche opened in its face.

nodes.task: A niche has opened in the slab — higher than a human stands. Take the tablet out of it and read it: right-click with the tablet in hand. Signs you understand read as words, the rest stay signs; click a line to work on its signs.
nodes.story: "Who comes looks into the sky. Who comes will find the road. The road goes by the stars." The slab is a mark for one who comes by the sky, and whoever cut its niche did not have to reach up. The next tablet lies where light rests on a dead world: its bright spot shows even in a telescope.

nodes.task: In the asteroid belt there is a small world with a spot that shines like a lamp somebody forgot to put out. In the heart of the spot stand mirrors: make the light reach the dark vault, and take what the vault keeps.
nodes.story: "Light goes by the mirrors. The mirror gives the light to the ring. Light wakes the ring." The mirrors led light to the gate rings — and stand three human heights tall on a world with no one to look into them. With the tablet lay the drawing of a lens that shows Ringwright signs and trails; the lens is lit by ring sparks. The third tablet is where life sleeps under ice.

nodes.task: Under the ice of a moon of Jupiter, on the floor of its ocean, lies something huge and dark: its lights show from afar through the water. Go down to it — the water there is heavy: shed the pressure in its air pockets. The niche in its heart stays silent until the four bells of the nave sing the song the whale sings: listen to it, and watch its lights.
nodes.story: "The hunger broke a world. The ark keeps life. Life sleeps under the ice." The whale, the crabs, the glowing mats were carried here out of a world broken by the same hunger that is named on the gates of the Hive and the Lament. The ark still sleeps; its doorways were not made for a human.

nodes.task: Once a day, out in space, the radio of your ship catches a narrow signal on the hydrogen line. When the strip "1420 MHz" appears in the uplink, turn the nose of the ship to where the signal grows and hold it there until the record is complete.
nodes.story: On August 15, 1977, the Big Ear radio telescope heard a narrow signal for 72 seconds — right on the hydrogen line, thirty times above the noise. The astronomer circled the printout "6EQUJ5" and wrote "Wow!" beside it. On Earth it was never heard again. Out here it comes every day, and always from the same side.

nodes.task: Rings of light hang over the places of the Ringwrights — the Monolith on the Moon is the first of them. A ring strikes whoever it sees with a beam: watch for the thin line it draws to you, step aside or behind stone, and hit it while it cools and its clasps stand open. Bring back a ring spark.
nodes.story: The rings do not wander and do not sleep: each keeps its post by a niche or a place, and the place raises a new one a minute or two after the last one falls. Their light does not go out — it curls into a spark that hums near anything the Ringwrights touched.

nodes.task: The innermost big moon of Jupiter never cools: its volcanoes throw sulfur into the sky. Somewhere among the lava lakes a bell is ringing. Find the place and pass its trial; the niche is there.
nodes.story: There is a second road, and it runs not by the stars but down, through the fire under the worlds. It was kept warm — and the warmth was somebody's to give.

nodes.task: Under the orange haze of the great moon of Saturn lie seas that are not water. In the largest of them stands a beacon. Reach it.
nodes.story: The road is marked by beacons — fourteen pulsing lights, each with its own rhythm: a map that brings one home. People sent the same map out of their system on a plate of gold.

nodes.task: A small white moon of Saturn sprays ice into space from four long cracks. The jets sing. Find where the song is loudest.
nodes.story: The roads have one voice: the hum of the first and commonest thing in the sky. The rings sleep; the voice does not. It is the signal your ship hears.

nodes.task: One moon of Uranus looks sewn together from pieces of different worlds. Where a bright chevron lies across it, look at its point.
nodes.story: Worlds were not only set in place — a broken one was sewn back together, and the thread was light. The seams of Miranda still show.

nodes.task: The great moon of Neptune runs backwards. A chain goes from its ice into its sky — each link the height of a tower. Follow the chain.
nodes.story: Triton was towed here and anchored: the other end of the chain is the storm anchor of Neptune. Each link is the height of a tower.
The Ring at the Edge leads not from world to world but out, to the stars. It has a warden, like every world. And something hungry was watching this road when the door was shut.

nodes.task: Where the Call of the First leads in the Interrift there is a nest: a bowl of end stone in a ring of egg-shaped cliffs, and over it the bones of the first dragon. Its breath still lies in the hollows. The skull is waiting for you: climb to it.
nodes.story: At the start of every road a warden was set: a trial, not a wall. Whoever set the wardens set the rings too. The dragon's eggs never hatched: the wardens were set once, and nobody came back to set new ones.

nodes.task: In the Interrift the tall people of the End have a home: a forest of chorus under three unfinished ring frames, and a long hall behind it. Walk the hall to its far wall. The hosts do not like being stared at.
nodes.story: The tall people of the End carried blocks for those who set the rings, and they carry them still. Three ring frames stand unfinished over their forest; the blocks for the rest are stacked and waiting. Whoever they were carried for has not come back.

nodes.task: Far beyond the Sun there is a star that dims for no reason — unevenly, for days at a time. Something hangs around it in many pieces; one of them keeps an archive. Walk the archive to its sanctum.
nodes.story: Something came out of a place with no stars — a hunger that eats light. Around this star hung a swarm of mirrors that gathered its light and sent it toward the middle of the sky. The hunger came for the light; the swarm is going dark.

nodes.task: Somewhere deep in the Interrift the rifts were made. Where the threads of the void are thickest, look for the frames they were woven on.
nodes.story: The dark road was woven through the void, and its thread was starlight. The hunger came along the roads toward the light — so the roads were sewn shut, from the far side.

nodes.task: Under the crust of the Depths there is a hollow where a sun hangs and does not go out. Go down to it.
nodes.story: The fire road kept the worlds warm, and that warmth was given away — to the hunger. One fire was kept back: the Nether Sun, the last hearth of a home whose owners this tablet does not name.

nodes.task: At the bottom of the fire road, past the threshold, somebody is still striking a hammer. Follow the sound.
nodes.story: In the Crucible the gate rings were forged and carried whole to every world at once. A ring is a door nine blocks across, and a door is cut to the height of whoever walks through it. Down below, a hammer still strikes.

nodes.task: In the places of the Underweave hang cords with knots. Take the Ringwright Lens in hand, find a cord and right-click it: the knots are numbers of the script.
nodes.story: What was meant to be read the Ringwrights cut in stone; what was meant to be counted they tied in cord. One knot for each dot of a number sign, a long knot for eight, a loop for the ring of sixteen. A cord hangs beside what it counts: at the eye of the Sargasso, at the empty scar, at a window of the Sheer, on the loom of the Sampler, at an anchor of the First Thread. Every reading is paid in void shards.

nodes.task: Read all five cords of the Underweave. The last one, at the anchor of the First Thread, gives itself up only after the string has sung a chord.
nodes.story: Sixteen threads in the warp. Thirteen roads sewn shut — one more than there are worlds behind them. Sewn from the heart toward the sky, all in one sleep. And one thread tied off not from here. The cords do not say who tied them, or against what. They only count — the way a count is kept by someone who expects it to be checked. The knots also kept a pattern: the Twin Image, a second ship of light beside your own.

nodes.task: The works of the Underdeep are stamped: the water intake of the Ringwoodite Sea, a wedge in the Bridgmanite Halls, an anchor over the Iron Ocean, ingots in the Core Quarry. Look at a stamp through the Ringwright Lens and right-click it.
nodes.story: A founder stamps the work: whose it is, what it is made of, how many were cast. These stamps are worn smooth; the iron keeps them only for the Lens. Every reading is paid in deep embers.

nodes.task: Read all five hallmarks of the Underdeep. Two of them are in the Core Quarry: on a stack of ingots on the terraces and at the bottom, by the sealed well.
nodes.story: Water for the rings was drawn from the sea in the stone. The stone of the rings is the heart of a world. A ring was forged for every world — and one more, for no world. The last casting was not a ring, and its hallmark was never finished: the place of the last stamp is smooth. Whoever worked here left in the middle of a line. The stamps also kept a casting: the Geodynamo, power from the turning of the iron itself.

nodes.task: Every tablet you have read hums when turned one way — the way the signal comes from. Read the three tablets of the first road and record the signal: their lines are drawn on the star map.
nodes.story: Three lines — from the Moon, from Ceres and from Europa — cross beyond Neptune, at the edge of the system. Something there is calling, and it calls on the frequency of the commonest thing in the sky. No gate leads there: the call is answered by ship.
